thereafter, the vidyā becomes perfected and remains constantly present in one's dreams.
In a dream, it reveals everything that is imagined within the mind;
therefore, O daughter of the mountain, hear from me the science of reviving the dead.
Having uttered the seed-syllable *amṛta* and the mantra *mṛtasañjīvanī*, || 10 ||
Then, after having joined one's own [mantras], one should subsequently raise the deceased; these two [steps constitute the rite]. || 11 ||
At the end of the wife of Vṛhadbhānu, she is renowned throughout the three worlds; this great vidyā is now asleep, remembered as the most essential of the essential. (12)
O Śāmbhavī, by merely reciting [this] one hundred and eight times daily, [one attains the goal].
Then that vidyā shall become the bestower of success, the reviver of the dead. || 14 ||

O Goddess of beautiful countenance, when one who has gone to the abode of Death, or even one who has come from the smoke of a funeral pyre, touches a corpse while muttering the mantra, [the rite succeeds]. 15.
One shall truly become long-lived; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
I shall now declare the Madhumatī Vidyā, which causes the enchantment of all. (16)
Having uttered "Śrī Madhumatī," [one says] "the attractor of the stationary and the moving" [and] "the directions, the stationary and the moving.
*Ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ svāhā*. This supreme Great Vidyā consists of eight and one (nine) syllables.
This vidyā, which attracts the three worlds, has been declared; it is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
If a person recites [this mantra] one hundred and eight times daily for one year, then the Great Vidyā, which illuminates all knowledge, becomes perfected. (18)
One may draw forth even Sumeru, the quarters, and the ocean;
likewise rivers, jewels, cities, women, mountains, and great trees.

And he knows substances that are unobtainable, even those situated in the netherworld (pātāla) and elsewhere; he also knows the locations of cities, current events, and the affairs of kings as well as their enemies. (20)
By reciting [this] a hundred times at night on one's bed, the practitioner attains perfection. || 21 ||
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, abode of the universe, be gracious, O Lord of pleasant countenance!
O Master, that which was asked and that which was heard—I now desire to hear it.
Behold the great vidyā, Avatī, which dispels all ignorance.
Īśvara said:
O lady of excellent hips, I shall declare the auspicious Padmāvatī-vidyā.
Having first extracted the Praṇava (Oṃ), one should place the Māyā-bīja (Hrīṃ) after it. (23)
O Goddess, one should extract the word "Padmāvatī" ending in the vocative case;
then, at the end, one should utter the pair [of words] "tell the news of the three worlds. (24)
O Dear One, this great vidyā, ending with "svāhā," has been described as a wish-fulfilling creeper;
one should recite it one hundred and eight times daily for two years.
Then the perfected Great Vidyā speaks everything to the practitioner;
staying upon the bed at night, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.

O Śaṅkarī, day by day that auspicious Vidyā Padmāvatī knows the news of the welfare of the world; she shall relate in a dream the accounts of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others, as well as the events of the three worlds. (27)
The Goddess said:
"I have heard the meritorious means of accomplishment spoken by Mahākāla;
now I desire to hear the supreme method of subjugation."
O Mahādeva, it is easy to accomplish yet brings about great and swift success.
Īśvara said:
Out of consideration for you, O Queen of the Gods, I shall speak; listen to that.
O Goddess, in the past I told you how the knowledge of yogis arises. (29)
In brief now, O Goddess, I shall tell it to you in detail;
it must always be guarded with effort amidst the throngs of the uninitiated (paśus).
On a Tuesday, during the Nakta-yoga, and on the new moon day (Amāvāsyā),
a man should write the name of his enemy and place it under the sole of his left foot.
O Goddess of gods, the wise practitioner should then recite the Vāgbhava mantra over her feet one hundred and eight times; O Goddess, by that means, the speaker shall be brought under control.
In a dispute or legal proceeding, the enemy becomes utterly mute;
O lovely woman, he becomes as inert as a serpent upon seeing Tārkṣya.
Having observed that very thing, the dull-witted disputant will undoubtedly be defeated;
likewise, I shall now explain another supreme method of subjugation.
By the power of which yoga one may bring the world under control:
having first extracted the Praṇava, [followed by] Sundarī and Bhairavī. (35)
O Goddess, from the word *yoginī*, [one should say] *rājā*, *prajā*, and *mahārathī*;
likewise, having uttered *vaśaṅkari*, one should then say *aṃ*, *iṃ*, and *ṛṃ*. (36)
The twenty-six-syllable mantra has been declared as a wish-fulfilling tree;
by means of this mantra, O Goddess, one may [consecrate] either oil or sandalwood.
O lady of beautiful countenance, one should place that oil, consecrated by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, upon the mouth;
O daughter of the Mountain, one should apply a tilaka mark on the forehead with that sandalwood paste.
O Goddess, having performed this rite for subjugating the world, if the most excellent practitioner beholds anyone, that person will undoubtedly come under his control. || 39 ||
By this very method, one may delude even the Lord of the Gods;
how much more so, O Goddess, human beings who are sovereign lords of the earth? (40)
Now it is said, O Great Goddess, that there is a supreme method of subjugation, which is most wonderful and deludes all the worlds, O Goddess. (41)
I shall first proclaim the mantra, which is hidden in all tantras:
having first extracted the Praṇava, one should utter the word "Rājamukhī. (42)
Having again uttered *Rājamukhī*, one should speak the two *māyā* seeds;
then, after that, the *kāmabīja*, followed by the two words "Devī Devī. (43)
Afterwards, O Goddess, [the words] "Mahādevī-pada" and "Devadevī," along with the vocative form "Deveśi"—these constitute the four-word [mantra]. (44)
"Bring everyone before me, bring them under my control, svāhā!
This great mantra, ending with *svāhā*, is the supreme bestower of total subjugation. (45)
O Maheśvarī, at dawn while remaining on his bed, the virtuous practitioner should wipe his face three times with his right hand while reciting this mantra.

O passionate woman, one should perform this daily for the sake of bringing the world under control; then this entire world, including all that is moving and unmoving, will certainly become submissive. (47)
The Goddess said:
"O Mahādeva, by your grace I have heard this ancient [teaching];
and the Vidyā known as Svāpnavatī has been explained and understood by me. (48)
Now I wish to hear whatever distinction there may be therein;
tell me that, O Mahādeva, if you have favor toward me. (49)
Īśvara said:
Listen, O wise one, I shall tell you of the supreme Vidyā known as Svāpnavatī.
Having first extracted the Praṇava, one should then extract the seed-syllable of the bride (Vadhū-bīja). (50)
O Daughter of the Mountain, this mantra beginning with the seed-syllable of Māyā and ending with Svāhā—
having eaten sacrificial food (haviṣyānna) during the day, one should recite it one thousand times at night.
Then, upon a pure bed, she indeed beholds in a dream,
O Supreme Goddess, everything that was thought of by her mind.
Now I shall further declare the supreme awakening from dreams, by the mere knowledge of which one knows everything with certainty. (53)
Having first uttered the *praṇava*, [the mantra] is "li hūṃ śūlapāṇaye svāhā. O lotus-eyed one, this great mantra has been declared to you.
All the ritual procedures are as before; now hear the prayer to be recited at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*).
Oṃ, salutation to the three-eyed one of the world, to the tawny-hued great soul;
salutation to Vāmadeva of beautiful form, the lord of dreams. || 55 ||

(52) "Tell me in a dream the truth regarding all matters, whether auspicious or inauspicious"—having thus made this prayer with the mantra, one knows everything according to its true nature (bhāvataḥ). 56.
Thus has this been told to you, O Goddess—the unsurpassed awakening through dreams, a supreme secret, most delightful, and an excellent means of subjugation. (57)
All this, O Great Goddess, bestows all-encompassing knowledge;
it has been served incessantly, O Great Goddess, by the Siddhas and Śaṅkaras. (58)
O Supreme Goddess, because everything spoken by all [beings] in all wombs is obtained through the grace of Madhumatī, one should therefore take refuge in you when making a request. 59.

O beloved of Śambhu, O Goddess, the recitation of the Svapnāvatī-vidyā and other mantras that has been described for one desiring success is to be performed according to the sequence of years; yet, O Goddess, it is taught that the attainment of the fruit occurs even without [the full duration of] such recitation.
By the power of the perfected vidyā, even the gods and asuras become well-perfected.
Thus has this perfectly secret and most wonderful [teaching] been told to you; it must be concealed from the wicked, the corrupt, and in the presence of common, ignorant folk. 62.
He who acts otherwise shall be devoured by the hosts of ḍākinīs;
therefore, it must be concealed with every effort, especially so.
One should give it to one who is peaceful, self-controlled, of noble birth, a yogi, devoted, free from sin, a practitioner, and a great soul. || 64 ||
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the glorious Yoginītantra, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The eighth chapter.
The Goddess said:
"I have indeed heard the entire means of accomplishment issuing from your lotus-like mouth—[a path] frequented by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, siddhas, and cāraṇas. (1)
It is a mass of supreme bliss, bestowing the splendors of bliss and other states;
it is the supreme further shore, supremely meritorious, pure, and the greatest of all.
O Mahādeva, you speak of the origin of the Yoginīs, which is difficult even for the three worlds to attain, and which is augmented solely by bliss.
Īśvara said:
O Śivā, everything that occurred between us in the past has been forgotten;
it was an ultimate secret, causing fear even to the gods and asuras.
O lady of beautiful limbs, O beloved of Śiva, listen as I shall speak in brief that which is ancient, most secret, the essence of essences, and higher than the highest. 5.
"O auspicious lady, you must keep this secret, just as one guards the womb from another man;
for at the end of the life of the cosmic egg, it will be entirely devoid of all living beings."
When the five principles beginning with Earth were established solely within Śiva,
O Maheśānī, there was nothing at all in the three worlds except for you and me.
In the meantime, O Maheśvarī, I asked you in jest: "Is my capacity greater, or is yours as well?"
Now, O Supreme Goddess, salutations to you! Within the circle of the universe, there is no place anywhere to stay; O beautiful one, where shall I remain? (9)
p. 54) Whatever has been done by me, all that has indeed passed away. O Divine One, I am always detached from the activities of worldly existence. (10)
"O Maheśvarī, now provide a place for yourself to stay.
Having heard this, the Goddess then had eyes reddened with anger.
That cruel and wicked woman spoke very harshly to me:
"O Lord, whatever you have always done while depending upon me... (12)
"O Mahādeva, it is certain that without me you would become a corpse;
for, O Maheśānī, all this has been pervaded by me through yoga. (13)
I have assumed the form of a calf through imagination; what capability do you possess?
I am always the one who has entered the state of being the cause, possessing the form of the Creator (or the Nurse).
I am neither an effect nor anything whatsoever; indeed, there is nothing that I do not always burn within the fire [of consciousness].
I am the supreme one, intent on meditation, yet I am also the perishable and the transcendent.
Having entered into the state of being an effect, I am eternally of the nature of primordial matter (prakṛti). || 15 ||
At that time, indeed, all beings beginning with Brahmā manifest;
this entire universe, including gods and moving creatures, is composed of my Māyā. 16.
“O Supreme Lord, my month has begun with the obstacle of distraction.
Having heard these words of his, which were as harsh as a thunderbolt and extremely terrible, [the Lord spoke]. (17)
She said nothing to that goddess; at that time, there arose a state of steadiness within her.
"O Goddess, I am always restrained by internal suffering. (18)
Then, O fair-faced one, having firmly resolved upon the means for your subjugation within his heart, he went to the western region of the universe.

Having gone there in the past, O Great Goddess, to a secluded and dreadful place, she [attained] joy by means of the ashes of her own body toward the Daitya, who had previously been neither seen nor heard of. (20)
The lord of the Dānavas was most terrible, wondrous, and possessed of a fearsome name;
he was ten million yojanas in extent and established upon thirty-two hundred thousand [yojanas].
With hands reaching ten million [yojanas], most terrible, with ten million blazing eyes, possessing fifty lakhs of faces, and enveloped by garlands of flames. || 22 ||
O Maheśvarī, having granted him the great siddhis beginning with aṇimā,
and having made that most formidable one equal to myself in all respects, [I departed].
"O Goddess, with a joyful mind I have come into your presence.
That lord of the Dānavas also remained there, having made his bed upon the ocean of water. (24)
Having fashioned two pillows from the Suvela and Velā mountains,
you then spoke to me, having understood the intent of my mind.
"Now, O Prajāpati, this vessel of the universe is devoid of life;
command me, O Mahādeva, O Śiva, and I shall behold it whole. (26)
Then, smiling within my mind and increasing your longing, I said to you, "O blessed lady, come to the western direction. (27)
O Goddess of Gods, having seen you elsewhere everywhere, I shall quickly [turn to] you;
for such is the nature of women, O Goddess of Gods, that they are drawn toward whoever stands below. 28.
"Upon seeing it, there would always be great faith and a desire to know;
knowing this, O Śivā, I spoke those words of prohibition. (29)

p. 56) Therefore, O Goddess of gods, because there is no further purpose for you, you remain by your own nature within Śiva; you have not gone elsewhere, but abide in my very presence—[and I abide in yours].
And in that great abode, the wilderness, resides Kedārakeśvara.
Having gone there, the Great Goddess, who causes the delusion of the world, [arrived].
He pierced the lord of the Daityas with thousands of love-arrows.
Thereupon, the lord of the Daityas, overwhelmed by the love-arrows, rose up,
stretched out all his arms, and spoke many flattering words.
Ghora said:
"Come to my lap; joyfully become the sovereign of all.
Save me, who am submerged in the ocean of passion, by the gift of your own body. (33)
"I cannot live for even a moment without you in any way;
O beautiful one, protect my life by embracing me with the devotion due to a husband. (34)
With such and other flattering words, he spoke to you again and again;
then you replied to him with a side-long glance and a pure smile. (35)
The Goddess said: "O lord of all Daityas, you are indeed the enjoyer of all; you are truly powerful, even among the hosts of gods.
You are heroic and the destroyer of all; we choose you as our protector if you will do so. (36)
Listen here to my story, for there shall be no place for me to stay;
indeed, fulfill that promise which was made by me in the past, if you are to take me with you.

"O King of the Daityas, it is indeed my resolve that he who shall stand having utterly defeated me in battle—he alone shall be my husband, and no other. Therefore, engage in combat with me from this point on. (38)
Īśvara said:
O Goddess, as you were speaking thus, he indeed rebuked you loudly with great wrath, with a voice as deep as the roar of the ocean at the time of universal dissolution. (39)
Then the terrible Kālarudra arose and was humbled;
at that time, the Daitya rushed forth to seize the entire world.
Nevertheless, he was in no way able to seize you;
then, through great speed of awakening, the lord of the Dānavas chanted [and went]. || 41 ||

By the force of his hand’s touch, those mountains were reduced to powder; by the touch of his hand, they were brought to a state of being grasped. From the blow of his foot, they ceased to exist and sank indeed into the ocean of waters.
By the wind of that great whirlpool, the mass of surging water rose up and fell down within the cauldron,
forming waves of extreme terror.
Pervading the entire universe, he wandered incessantly;
desiring to grasp that Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), he became unable to grasp her. (44)
Only the preeminent among gods beheld you at every step;
whatever battle was fought by him cannot even be described.
O Śivā, whatever was hurled at you has all been reduced to ashes by your splendor, O Maheśānī; yet even so, he remained overcome with rage.
The terrible Daitya of fearsome prowess became continuous [as he continued] without interruption.
Listen, O Goddess of gods, to the wonderful and most brilliant battle that took place. (47)
From the water-born cauldron, however, smoke arises intensely, and [consciousness] emerges. 48.
O Maheśānī, at that time during the battle, overcome by fear, I resorted to yoga and assumed a body more subtle than the subtlest. (49)
O Supreme Goddess, having performed [this rite] and always remaining dependent upon you,
the king of the Daityas was then unable to strike you down by any means whatsoever.
And he indeed reflected upon various means to kill you, having enlarged his own body and rubbed it against your arm. (51)
"I shall slay you, a great villain, in a cauldron"—having thus reflected in his mind and having swollen his body, [he spoke]. (52)
The entire universe was filled by him, and the terrible Daitya attained great joy;
he then said to you, "O slain one, where will you go?"
Beholding the Daitya filling the entire universe, you said to him: "O terrible Daitya, stay! Stay, O evil-minded one! (54)
"How have you come to be separated? I shall slay you with joy!
O great wicked one, you did not recognize me at any time until this very moment. (55)
From me the creation has arisen; it dissolves back into me alone. By me alone is everything protected—this world which consists of my own māyā. (56)
Other than Me there is nothing else; I am the eternal Brahman itself.
Listen, O best of fools, to our supreme and great auspiciousness. 57.
O Daitya, whether they worship me with a wicked disposition or again with a virtuous disposition, I grant them their desires exactly as they are.
"I grant you a cause that yields great and unsurpassed fruit;
O Daitya, there is no doubt that I have been served by you for a long time. (59)
(59) With a single-minded focus, you have exerted yourself here for my sake; you are Śiva, of this there is no doubt, since whatever delusion you had was caused by me. (60)
Now behold my form, the supreme state of Brahman-bliss, seeing which no one shall ever manifest again. (61)
O Lord, hear this: that supreme form of Śiva which you meditated upon as being deficient—that very form is the supreme abode; it is the form of Kālī. (62)
"Beyond this, there is no form of Brahman anywhere else," having said this, O Goddess Bhavānī, the liberator from worldly existence, I then spoke.
O Supreme Goddess, when I, speaking as Kālī, meditated upon that supreme form,
you were then born repeatedly as Kālikā.
She is black in color, most terrible, and stands upon Mahākāla;
she is adorned with a garland of severed heads, beautiful with her folds [of skin], with disheveled hair and a smiling face. (65)
Adorned with the tongues of the world and three fierce red eyes,
she shines with the radiance of the digit of the new moon, her form blazing with a crown.
Accompanied by thousands of crores of jackals arising from the circle of fire,
they proceeded in the four directions with great roars and terrible prowess.
Yoginīs arising in multitudes from the mass of rays, numbering in the tens of millions, stand on all sides in terrible forms, intensely eager for the great battle. (68)
O Goddess, within the center of the inverted cavity, millions upon millions of cosmic eggs shine forth eternally, and they are all composed of the sun. 69.
Having thus seen Kālikā, the lord of the Dānavas fainted;
yet, upon seeing the beautiful orb of Mahākālī’s face, he was filled with confidence.
At that very moment, the lord of the Dānavas attained the knowledge of Brahman.
Then, seeing that lord of the Dānavas devoted to knowledge and perfectly pure, [he spoke]. (71)
"O Mother, with my flickering tongue I shall cut up Kālī in the midst of battle; having devoured her along with the entire universe, I shall die in an instant. (72)
Kālī, intensely eager for the great sound of terrible instruments, acted with restless playfulness; she was always pervading the vast banners of various machines.
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the Yoginītantra, the Great King of Tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The ninth chapter.
Īśvara said:
Having seen that great marvel, my mind overwhelmed with fear, I suddenly went to that supreme wilderness. || 1 ||
O Goddess, having indeed gone there by way of the Suṣumnā path,
whatever was seen and heard by me cannot possibly be told.
O Goddess, this which consists of every marvel has been pointed out; it has never been seen or heard of anywhere.
There are exceedingly vast cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas) by the millions upon millions.
O Goddess, they always move about; who would be able to enumerate them?
O Goddess, they have millions upon millions of faces and likewise millions upon millions of arms;
such are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others, appearing in various forms.
(61) Endowed with great sovereignty, the inhabitants of every Brahmāṇḍa, O Goddess, having beheld that which consists of all wonders, became joyful in mind. || 5 ||
Everything has become forgotten by me; who am I, absorbed as I am in anxiety? Who am I, from where have I come, and why does no one ask about me anywhere? (6)
"O Goddess, in this way, I am always forgetful within this world;
there is never a time when the confusion of various places is not being remembered by me. (7)
Then, at the end of ten million years, you reached my heart-lotus;
having gone there, I beheld everything, wondrous and beautiful.
O Supreme Goddess, it is impossible to describe all of that;
for this scripture, which brings about the rise of one's own dharma and purpose, is the cause of both worldly happiness and liberation.
The Vedas are his supreme self; the individual soul is his vision; the senses are his sight; the body is the Purāṇa; and whatever Smṛtis there may be are his limbs. (10)
In that very place, O fair-faced one, all the scriptures, beginning with the *Lomaharṣaṇīya*,
[teach] that just as there is no difference between the individual soul (*jīva*) and the Self (*ātman*), so too is there no difference among the various Āgamas.

Having beheld the auspicious row of letters, consisting of intense radiance, within the heart-lotus—at the tip of the petals, in the middle of the petals, and at the edge of the petals—may it proceed. 12.
Grammar, ritual manuals, etymology, prosody, and all other minor treatises whatsoever. (13)
"But I have told you that I was born in the world of Pūrṇabala; therefore, O Goddess, within the pericarp [of my heart], there is a hundred-fold, most brilliantly radiant [light]. (14)
(62) It blazes with tens of millions upon tens of millions of suns and moons, and is adorned by a circle of splendor from tens of millions upon tens of millions of great fires. || 15 ||
In the midst of that, I beheld a mass of light, exceedingly brilliant,
possessing the radiance of ten million suns and the coolness of ten million moons.
Blazing with the splendor of ten million fires, it is eternal and composed of the Supreme Brahman.
O Goddess, it is always composed of all-knowledge and consists of all wonders;
O Goddess, it is always composed of all sacrifices and consists of all sacred fords. || 18 ||
O Goddess, it consists of all merit, and likewise of all dharmas;
O Goddess, it consists of the knowledge of Brahman, and likewise of the bliss of Brahman. || 19 ||
O Maheśvarī, it is the authority for all scriptures, beginning with the Vedas;
it is the authority for all living beings, the supreme Brahman-splendor that is most beneficial.
O Goddess, it is forever beyond all illusion, the cutter away of all illusion,
consisting of all bliss, and composed of the knowledge of Brahman (or the bliss of Brahman).
O Goddess, it consists of full bliss, the supreme Brahman-nirvāṇa;
O Goddess, it is composed of all māyā and, moreover, composed of all vidyā.
O Goddess, it consists entirely of austerity, and likewise it consists entirely of all spiritual accomplishments;
O Goddess, it consists entirely of all liberation, and likewise it consists entirely of all the Vedas.
O Goddess, it consists of all the worlds, and likewise it consists of all enjoyments;
O Goddess, it consists of all the scriptures, and likewise it consists of all yogas.
Having seen this scripture there, in that ocean blinded by my own ignorance,
I then beheld it as clearly as the dawn at sunrise.
(63) Indeed, everything has been mastered by me through the grace of Mahākālī;
having seen it, everything was mastered by me at that very moment—there is no doubt regarding this, which possesses a splendor equal to the sun’s radiance. || 26 ||
Then, having gone among the clusters of filaments, I indeed beheld it.
O Goddess, it consists of a multitude of colors and possesses a radiance equal to the light of the sun;
furthermore, it includes Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, Sāṃkhya, and likewise Pātañjala.
Indeed, at that very moment, I understood the Vaiśeṣika [doctrine] as it was before;
then, having seen the sequence of letters from the region near the edge of the pericarp. (29)
Possessing a radiance equal to a hundred suns and causing delight to all,
the Ayurveda and the science of medicine were indeed mastered by me at that very time.
In that interval, O Great Goddess, a beautiful series of letters was seen,
resembling a thousand suns, appearing as the color of a Śūdra and exceedingly radiant.
O Goddess of gods, the Smṛtis, Itihāsas, and Purāṇas were likewise studied by me;
indeed, all of that was mastered by me in a single moment—of this there is no doubt. (32)
Nevertheless, my deluded body is never purified;
within it, there remains that which was seen, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns.
O Goddess, this knowledge of Brahman, enveloped by the splendor of Brahman, is renowned as Vedānta; it possesses the great radiance of a multitude of letters. (34)
That great [state] was practiced by me for a moment, yet through delusion it slipped away from those superior beings;
in that interval, I beheld something blazing with a mass of colors.
Resembling ten million suns and as cool as ten million moons,
O Goddess, it is eternally composed of all knowledge and embodies all sacred pilgrimage sites.
(64) O Goddess, it consists of all sacrifices and likewise consists of all dharmas;
O Maheśvarī, it is the authority for all living beings, including the scriptures and other such works. (37)
The four Vedas—the Sāma, Atharva, Ṛg, and the most excellent Yajus—all of them were indeed studied by me at that very moment; of this there is no doubt. (38)
Nevertheless, no satisfaction arises in me, nor does it come at that very moment;
for I am indeed composed of all knowledge, all reality, and all accomplishments.
Then, O Goddess, you— Kālī, the eternal one, dancing in the form of Brahman, accompanied by auspicious Yoginīs— were saluted by them. Thereafter,
having reached Uḍḍīna, you arrived at Dvidala along with me.
O Maheśvarī, when Mahākālī was at the wheel of command (ājñācakra) between my eyebrows,
my memory then returned regarding Brahmā and Viṣṇu once again.
O Great Goddess, at the time of that dance, two drops of sweat fell from Kālī’s chin; from those two, the two [sons] worthy of their qualities were born. (42)
Seeing them with their bodies trembling from fear, Brahmā and Viṣṇu then quickly entered the two nostrils.
Then, O Maheśvarī, Dhātṛ arrived at Piṅgalā at daybreak;
thereafter Viṣṇu went to Īḍā, and having gone there, he [joined] those two auspicious ones.
O Goddess, having repeatedly witnessed these many great and wondrous transformations, and seeing us with our teeth intact, what could possibly have been forgotten? (45)
(65) O Maheśānī, thus conversing and wandering here and there, those two lords were afflicted with great sorrow.
O Great Goddess, having learned that Viṣṇu had previously gone there,
I gave him knowledge and a most auspicious mantra.
At that very moment, he became my equal and was entirely like my left limb;
to him I imparted all the scriptures through mere speech, without the need for traditional transmission (āgama).
Seated upon Garuḍa, Mahāviṣṇu became joyful and robust;
taking him with him, the Supreme Lord went there to the cosmic egg (Brahmāṇḍa).
Having gone to him, O Great Goddess, I gave him that most wonderful mantra;
at that very moment, O Great Goddess, he became the Grandfather (Brahmā) endowed with supreme knowledge.
O Supreme Goddess, by my command at that time, he was born as my very own right limb, equal to me, and as the Creator (Brahmā).
Viṣṇu bestowed upon him all the Śāstras, as well as the Veda-Śāstra, which makes one proficient; then Brahmā, freed from distress, was indeed forever joyful, nourished, and contented.
Therefore, O Maheśvarī, you indeed remain forever my first preceptor; having accepted that knowledge along with those two [disciples], [you have done so].
Yesterday, I went here and there in various ways, intent upon the great dance with auspicious yoginīs. (54)
For a hundred crores of divine years, she who is the Supreme Self danced with great joy amidst various musical instruments, singing songs adorned with diverse ornaments. (55)

With flowers resembling the moon, the sun, fire, and the soma-plant, and with various blossoms— both those rising up and those falling— that possessed divine fragrances, she was filled with great longing.
O Goddess, it is always secluded from the range of vision by those intent on dance, and it is colored by hundreds of banners equal in size to the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa). (57)
Having been seen and trampled by many diverse [beings],
we have therefore begun to praise Kālī Karālikā.
With eyes overflowing with tears, speech faltering, and heads bowed, he then praised the Creator with devotion using all the scriptures, joining his palms in reverence. (59)
O Maheśānī, Parā then spoke to Koṭivarṣa:
"Alas, O Creator, you have forgotten the meaning of all the scriptures, even though such are your qualities! (60)
"You are the knower of investigation; always be the creator. Thus commanded, the Creator then felt his purpose was fulfilled.
Then Mahāviṣṇu praised the consort of Śambhu with all the Vedas;
after ten koṭis of years had passed, Śivā spoke this to Viṣṇu. Then Śivā said to him: || 62 ||
O Mahāviṣṇu, you are a knower of the Vedas; you are my devotee, an abode of virtues;
you are a knower of dharma; be a protector and a guardian of creation. || 63 ||
Having thus placed this command upon his head, he, who is devoted to the welfare of the world, felt his purpose fulfilled;
thereafter, [he beheld] Kālī, the supreme, eternal, and primordial Brahman.
With supreme devotion, he praised the Great Goddess according to the sacred tradition;
then, after twenty crore years, she spoke to me.
Kālī said:
O Sadāśiva, you who know the scriptures and possess great wisdom, you are eternally free from the physical body;
as a great yogi endowed with attributes, become the creator and destroyer.
Having thus placed her command upon my head, I praised her once more;
then she spoke to me for five hundred million divine years.
O Sadāśiva, I am praised by them in the Āgamas and I am pleased with you.
O Mahādeva, what is requested? I shall grant it; there is no doubt in this.
Īśvara said:
O Mother, I abide eternally within the lotus of your feet.
Kālī said:
"Whatever kind of battle was fought by me against the Dānava named Ghora, he will indeed fight a battle that is but a ten-millionth part of what I have done. (70)
O Lord of Gods, born from the womb of a buffalo and produced from your seed, he (you) shall become the one who bears the name Mahiṣāsura.
Having assumed an asuric nature, he will wage a great war;
then, having destroyed him, I shall manifest in my true form as Bhadrakālī.
"I shall place my left big toe upon your heart-lotus;
from now on, O Mahādeva, you shall always remain beneath the sole of my foot. (73)
"Stay here in the form of a Śabara and occupy my seat.
Having been thus commanded by the Goddess, we fell at the vicinity of her feet. (74)
Then, as he prostrated himself like a staff, a hundred thousand years passed;
right there, Kālī, whose form is consciousness and who is the partless Brahman, vanished.
Thus has the detailed account of the origin of the Yoginī been told to you;
this supreme treasure, together with its ritual methods, must be guarded with great effort by all. (76)
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The tenth chapter.
Īśvara said: O Goddess, having risen again and not seeing you, we,
speaking while deeply afflicted by grief, were submerged once more in an ocean of sorrow.
Alas, Mother! Your lotus-face surpasses ten million moons and suns;
what is this red dye upon your feet, which is a mass of the ocean of compassion? (2)
The vast and supreme form that deludes through great illusion—what is it but the most auspicious light of the moons upon her nails? (3)
O Mother, what has become of that wondrous sight, with its millions upon millions of lunar discs dripping from its mouths; what will become of it, and where has this marvel gone?

Alas, alas, O Mother! This form of yours, which is imperishable and consists of existence, consciousness, and bliss—we no longer perceive it as such, because of our attitude toward you as a mere mother. || 5 ||
Deprived of our mother and father, we children wander about;
and having wept again and again, we all remain here calling out in that manner.
O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, O Lotus-eyed One, through such various lamentations as these, we were brought to five hundred thousand years.
Having wept, they rose up again and, wailing loudly and intensely, cried:
"O Mother, where have you gone? Where have you departed? What will become of us? (8)
How is it that you have cast us away into this sea so difficult to cross?
Alas, O Mother, you have no compassion; we are but wretched children! (9)
If you do not protect us, who indeed will protect us?
Apart from you, there is no mother, nor is there even a father for us. (10)
"We shall surely die if we do not see you; this is the firm and certain truth. For a child deprived of both mother and father, life itself is impossible."
"How is this so, O Mother? Let it be known by yourself indeed. (11)

"Free from longing, our compassion for him has arisen; therefore, direct your compassion toward that compassion which arose in him. Then the Yoginī spoke words raining down the great nectar of immortality: || 12 ||
Kālī said: "O Maheśāna, let not the highly fortunate Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara be afflicted by fear;
I shall always remain among them. Thus she spoke then, indeed as the imperishable one.
I am of the nature of truth, consciousness, and bliss; I am indeed Brahman, the radiantly shining light.
There is never any destruction of me; remain free from doubt. 14.
Having meditated upon that form which has been seen by us and is considered supreme by you—pure in nature—recite my mantra. (15)
That very [act] shall become a highly radiant auspiciousness for you;
now enter the body of Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, and remain firm.
Oho! Great Lord, Lord of Gods, please enter the body of Brahmā, while the Lord performs this creation consisting of knowledge and action.
Īśvara said:
Having spoken thus, that Mahākālī, the consort of Śambhu, bestowed upon us the powers of will, knowledge, and action, which accomplish all tasks and purposes. (18)
Desire was given to Viṣṇu, while the power of action was given to Brahmā;
having bestowed upon me the power of knowledge, she who is the embodiment of all powers [departed]. (19)
Kālī said: Then Mahākālī spoke: "Listen, O supreme lords;
I shall enter into you in my full form, O Śaṅkara. (20)
This very one is the Guru, the God, the illustrious Śiva, the Supreme Lord;
for he alone is the speaker of the scriptures, and neither Brahmā nor Viṣṇu is so.
"For I am indeed the learned one among all of you; of this there is no doubt.
I shall delude Brahmā, Viṣṇu, or even Maheśvara. (22)
Īśvara said:
Having spoken thus, that Mahākālī entered into us,
and at that time this Mādhava entered the body of Brahmā.
Then he deluded that Brahmā, who was the embodiment of Brahman;
thereupon Brahmā himself, having realized this, personally offered the imperishable oblation.
At that time, he attained the renown of being "Svayambhū" (Self-Existent), of this there is no doubt;
yet he was overwhelmed with anxiety, thinking, "What shall I do? Where shall I go? (25).
In this very manner, that Creator, having dwelt for a full year,
first emitted water alone— pervasive, supreme, and vast.
That water, consisting of the conceit of qualities, was the manifest ocean of causes;
abiding therein, he produced gold as his form and the accumulation of waters as his vigor.
As many as those bubbles of its potency arise in the vicinity,
so many are declared to be cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas), floating in the ocean of the primal cause.
O Goddess, assuming the form of Rudra himself, I constantly bring about the dissolution of the various cosmic eggs for the sake of protecting each respective universe. (29)
O Great Goddess, O Śivā, with the trident in my hand, I stand eternally by the side of every single universe in the form of each individual Rudra.
Just as the union of two cosmic eggs never occurs,
so do I remain constantly within that causal ocean, acting in such a way.
In this very same way, all of us—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—reside within every Brahmāṇḍa; there is no doubt about this.
Then Brahmā, the sustainer of the world, having entered into each of the other four principles (tattvas) individually from within the center of every universe, [proceeded]. (33)
He created earth, fire, wind, and space;
by means of these five elements, he brought about the entire creation. || 34 ||
Then, by the will of Brahmā, the Blessed Viṣṇu emerged from the body of Brahmā and protected her forever.
O Goddess, by the command of Brahmā, having assumed the form of Viṣṇu with mighty arms within each individual universe,
I repeatedly bring about creation and destruction within the interior of every universe.
For I, O Supreme Goddess, have taken refuge in the body of Brahmā. || 38 ||
Thus, O Brahmā, you do not remember anything; O Maheśvarī, you do not remember anything.
Indeed, the Treasure of the World knows that every action belongs to me alone. (39)
O Goddess, all principles such as water, the entire expansion beginning with the cosmic egg,
all beings beginning with the gods, the cardinal and intermediate directions, and all that is moving and unmoving— [all this is pervaded by me].
O Goddess, Brahmā knows everything—the effect, the cause, as well as the origin of Viṣṇu—and furthermore, he understands through my illusory power (māyā) that which is performed by me. (41)
But all this is indeed false; it is merely the mother’s illusion (māyā). Those men who resort to that very illusion [and reach its further shore], they cross over this illusion. 42.
If that supreme Māyā is angry, she bestows mere liberation;
if she herself is angry, she, as my mother, bestows the yoga of the stages (bhūmi). || 43 ||
O Goddess, for him liberation is dependent upon his lotus feet;
for him my Great Goddess, Maheśvarī, my mother, is pleased. O Great Goddess, for him my mother Kālikā is indeed pleased and has taken refuge at his feet as a devoted servant.
The Goddess said:
"O God, O Maheśvara, by your grace I have indeed heard everything;
yet there remains one part of the entire account that has not been heard, which is beyond the reach of Brahmā and the other gods. (45)
Now I wish to hear that which was spoken regarding the Ocean of Causes.
O Mahādeva, tell me what is the thing to be supported, what is the support, and what is that which supports it;
O Lord of Gods, tell me the boundary if you have affection for me.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim that which is auspicious, more secret than the secret; for it is to be strictly guarded, most hidden, and beyond the reach of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others.
O Goddess, Mahākāla Maheśvara would become the great ocean. || 49 ||
For she, whose form was empty, imagined a husband for the sake of sport. || 50 ||
She herself is Kālī, the Mother of the World, and she is equal to Mahākāla; having assumed a form of half-luster, she bears Mahākāla within her. (51)
Of empty form and black color, she is intoxicated and possesses the upward radiance (*ūrdhvataijasī*).
O Goddess, you have asked about the boundary (*sīmā*); that very boundary is Brahman alone. (52)
The splendor of Brahman is of the nature of light, and likewise its form is that of illumination;
that light, O Great Goddess, is devoid of both the pervaded and the pervader.
There is neither the superimposed nor the substratum; it is non-dual and without interval.
For all this, O Goddess, is entirely composed of māyā. (54)
O Goddess, everything is indeed false; only Brahman alone is real.
This which has been told to you is the essence of essences, higher than the highest. (55)
O Maheśvarī, this is the secret more secret than the secret, the secret within secrets;
for this is the supreme knowledge that cuts through all illusion.

Consisting of all-encompassing knowledge, this is considered the division [of the teaching] whose form is the Great Sun; it is superior to ten million times ten million great gifts and ten million times ten million great austerities. (57)

O Maheśvarī, from ten million times ten million great knowledges, from ten million times ten million great vows, and from plunging into—indeed, bathing in—ten million times ten million great sacred fords; || 58 ||
But if, after many births have passed, one should ever hear [this], then, O Goddess, one shall be liberated and shall not be born again in saṃsāra. || 59 ||
Thus has this been told to you; guard it like your own womb.
Act with such effort that no one else may obtain it in this way. 60.
It must be guarded, guarded, guarded with great effort;
it must be guarded with diligence, for it is my most excellent and supreme treasure.
One should give [the teaching] to one who is peaceful, steadfast, a yogin, a kula-yogin, and a man of knowledge, O Goddess of the God of Gods; otherwise, one shall go to hell. (62)
O Goddess, whose eyes are like darting wagtails, I have told you the essence, the knowledge of Brahman. What more do you wish to hear?
"There is nothing superior to this in my mind;
it must always be kept secret, O auspicious lady, in the presence of cattle-herders and common folk. (64)
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The eleventh chapter. The Goddess said:
O God, worshipped by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, and the lords of the asuras!
O Lord of Gaṇeśa, Nandin, and Candreśa, who art saluted by Govinda and Brahmā! || 1 ||
O Lord whose feet are worshipped by the masters of yoga, O Teacher of all the worlds, remove [my sins]!
That which is called the supreme knowledge, Kālī, the destroyer of impurities—[that I shall now declare]. 2.
Whatever mantra, means of accomplishment, worship, preliminary rite, mudrā, offering, as well as fire-oblation, mental disposition, and likewise the location; || 3 ||
I have previously heard her meditation, hymn of praise, and armor;
now, O Maheśvara, I desire to hear about her abode and her divisions.
O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, by your grace tell me instantly: where is liberation attained, or where is the supreme accomplishment found? (5)
O Supreme Lord, when the world relies upon this [system], it quickly becomes a partaker of the fruits of its own actions, having indeed abandoned the excessive labor [of other methods]. (6)
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall describe that place which is extremely difficult to attain;
it brings about swift accomplishment, O Goddess, and bestows the fruit of supreme liberation. (7)
Indeed, no place other than the Kālikā cremation ground is praised;
whatever action is performed there, one shall obtain its infinite fruit. (8)
And if, O Supreme Goddess, even a single *puraścaryā* is performed there, it is not so; for, O Great Goddess, he who is endowed with devotion and possessed of power [is truly successful]. (9)
The accomplishment of the mantra will certainly occur; there is no wonder whatsoever in this.
Worship, yielding infinite fruit, is effective everywhere, both in water and on land.
O Goddess, whether it be through the divine aspect (divyabhāva), or through the heroic aspect (vīrabhāva), or likewise the Śākta, Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, or even another [tradition]. (11)
O fair-faced one, whoever should recite [this] in Vārāṇasī for the duration of a single month, beginning at the time of dawn until midday; || 12 ||
The accomplishment of the mantra will certainly occur; this is the truth that grants perfect success.
O Goddess of gods, O Śivā, liberation will necessarily arise for him.
O Goddess of gods, there is Mahāśmaśāna as well as Ānandakānana;
O Great Goddess, there is Avimukta and again Gaurīmukha. (14)
(76) Vārāṇasī is the great sacred field, the form of Kālī, higher than the highest.
O Goddess, what can I tell you of whatever is performed there? 15.
In Kāmarūpa, there is a great worship that bestows the fruit of all accomplishments; likewise at the Golden Mountain of Nepal and the confluence of the Brahmaputra. (16)
Relying upon the Karatoyā river as far as the region of Dikkaravāsinī,
there is Kuñjagiri to the north and to the west of the Karatoyā.
O best of holy places, O daughter of the mountain, you are a river in the eastern direction;
in the south, you extend as far as the confluence of the Brahmaputra and the Lākṣā.
He is known as Kāmarūpa, as is certain in all the scriptures, for his mind becomes serene in order to discharge the three debts. (19)
If even a single person goes there, having undertaken a pilgrimage, he should proceed with supreme devotion to the vicinity of the womb of Kāmākhyā.
At every step, a person obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice;
[the field] is thirty yojanas wide and one hundred yojanas in length. || 21 ||
Know that Kāmarūpa is of supreme triangular form;
Kedāra is in the northeast, and Gajaśāsana is in the northwest. || 22 ||
O Goddess, at the confluence on the south, where the lac-dye and the seed of Brahmā meet,
know that very place to be a triangle, saluted by gods and asuras alike.
In that place, those who are humans are indeed gods; of this there is no doubt.
And whatever water is there, O Goddess, all of that is surely a sacred ford (tīrtha).
The upavīthi, the vīthi, the upapīṭha, the pīṭhaka, the siddhapīṭha, the mahāpīṭha, and within that, the brahmapīṭha. || 25 ||
(77) O Great Goddess, the Viṣṇu-pīṭha is there, and within that is the Rudra-pīṭha;
it is known as the Ninefold Womb (navayoni), extending in all directions throughout the four quarters. || 26 ||
In each of those places, there is a great worship that yields progressively superior fruits;
O auspicious lady, it is certain that the fruit is thus doubled, doubled. (27)
For all branches of knowledge and for every mantra of Śambhu, the fruit of worship and recitation is indeed doubled, doubled. 28.
The nine wombs have been fully described, as well as the circle of the womb known as Kāmākhya;
[the region] from Āyoni up to Mahī, and extending as far as the Gandhamādana mountain of ignorance.
O Goddess, this [place] extending five krośas is difficult for all to attain;
it is most wonderful and is served by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the other gods. (30)
Even the gods desire death; what then to say of humans?
O Maheśānī, O Śivā, within this five-krośa expanse of the Yonipīṭha! 31.
Those who go toward the auspicious state, having died, are not subject to rebirth;
and they never again encounter the affliction that has the nature of the sun.
And those best of men who dwell at the sacred seat of Yonipīṭha, being free from sin, have all become Śaṅkaras, three-eyed and with the moon upon their crests. || 33 ||
O Goddess, the most excellent practitioner performs the worship and the recitation of all sciences and of every mantra. || 34 ||
A man becomes the locus of the eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇiman*;
and in the midst of that, O Great Goddess, there is a mountain resplendent as a blue mountain (*nīlācala*). (35)
Furthermore, O Supreme Goddess, he possesses the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva and consists of all powers;
in the midst of that is the supreme secret cave of the mind-born [Kāma].
Within the cave of the mind, she who takes the form of the blood-drinking water, Kāmākhyā—the wish-fulfilling creeper—is surrounded by ten million liṅgas. (37)
Her cave of the mind is perpetually inflamed by that splendor;
by the mere touch of it, iron attains the state of gold. (38)
O Daughter of the Mountain, it measures four cubits on all sides;
by the mere touch of this [liṅga], a human being attains the state of Śiva. (39)
O Goddess, one becomes sinless at that very moment; of this there is no doubt.
Whatever action is performed here, its fruit shall be infinite. (40)
In the midst of that, O Supreme Goddess, extending twelve finger-breadths on all sides from the netherworld (pātāla) upwards, O Goddess, is a lake consisting of a mass of surging water.
O Supreme Goddess, that water consists of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; O Goddess, that divine water is known as the Ocean of Causes (Kāraṇārṇava).
O Goddess, what need is there for much speaking? That water is the supreme nectar; O beautiful Mother, know this as it has been told through a secret convention. 43.
O Goddess, all beings, both moving and stationary, constantly long for that water;
by the mere touch of that water and by touching that lake, [they are purified]. 44.
O Goddess, at that very moment the human certainly becomes a god;
freed from both merit and sin, he will surely become liberated while living. (45)
O Maheśvarī, whoever indeed worships in that lake with its water—even with thousands of crores of tongues or hundreds of crores of mouths—[attains the fruit]. 46.
O Daughter of the Mountain, O Maheśvarī, I am not at all able to describe that fruit, even as one might reach out a hand into a lake and grasp the water within it. 47.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one becomes a master of great siddhis on earth;
for him, the accomplishment of the mantra occurs at that very moment—of this there is no doubt. (48)
O Maheśvarī, whether they be Śaivas, Vaiṣṇavas, Śāktas, or others,
those who indeed chant this mantra attain perfection at that very moment.

There is no need for deliberation even regarding one who offers water to the ancestors with a hundred and eight blades of kusha grass, even if that water has been drawn up by the tips of those blades.
O Maheśvarī, by him half a million Gayā-śrāddhas have been performed.
Thus, O Goddess, this Kāmākhyā-yonimaṇḍala has been described to you.
O Maheśānī, I shall speak thus in brief and with particular detail;
however, O illustrious Goddess, its greatness is being told to you. 52.
Where Kālī, Tāriṇī, Chinnamastā, and Bhairavī—each divided into seven times seven—dwell together with ten million yoginīs. (53)
Dhūmā, Bhuvaneśānī, Mātaṅgī, Kamalālayā, Bhagaklinnā, Bhagādhārā, and likewise Bhagandarī. (54)
Durgā, Jayadurgā, and likewise Mahiṣamardinī—by all those very ones who have been declared as the secondary sciences (upavidyās). || 55 ||
Mahākālī dwells eternally there with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the other gods;
this sacred seat (pīṭha), which has the face of Brahmā as its support, has Ugratārā as its presiding deity.
That seat (pīṭha) is said to be manifold, O Maheśvarī, being both manifest and hidden;
the hidden is more meritorious than the manifest and is difficult to attain even for the most excellent practitioners.
O Goddess, it is found everywhere by those proficient in the two lineages (kula), within the fire of the cave of the mind-born [Kāmadeva], at the lofty peak of the Goddess. 58.
That pīṭha, known as Mahogram, is extremely difficult to attain.
The deity there is Bhuvaneśvarī, who is the form of Brahman and the Siddhi Kālī. (59)
There dwells Kālī, the destroyer of the terrible Daityas;
having sat upon that seat (pīṭha), one should recite the mantra ten times.
Then there shall be the purification of the mantra, and by means of that body one becomes Śiva.
That moment which I have described to you, O fair-eyed one, occurs indeed within the center of the heart.
The fruit of that [practice] would be deficient by one quarter, whereas in the recitation and worship of Śiva it is complete.
Arghya is to be known as being at Jālandhara, and at Uḍḍīyāna it is half of that.
The accomplishment of the tantra will certainly occur in Nepal by means of the lunar day and the day of the week near Nīlakaṇṭha; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (63)
O God, O Queen of the Gods, I have joyfully told you this regarding the mantra-recitation:
great accomplishment is attained on the thirteenth day, as well as in the forest of Ekābhra.
O Śivā, success is certain at Gaṅgā with ten lakhs;
O Daughter of the Mountain, it is attained swiftly at Rāḍhā and Vikaṭākṣā. (65)
Success shall be achieved with three hundred thousand [recitations]; this is indeed the truth for the attainment of perfect accomplishment.
At the place called Puṣkara, it is achieved with one hundred thousand, and through twenty hundred thousand in the ritual application.
O Śivā, by reciting it ten million times on Mount Droṇa and at Jvālā,
and likewise twelve hundred thousand times in the sacred field of Virajā, [one attains the goal].
In the Himalayas, [the fruit is obtained] by three hundred thousand; at Kedāra, by five hundred thousand;
on Kailāsa, by ten hundred thousand; and at Jayantī, by five hundred thousand.
O Śivā, through recitation and worship, the accomplishment of the mantra will certainly occur in Ujjayinī within ten days, and on Mount Mandara within a month.
Thus has that which was asked by you, O daughter of the mountain, been told to you. O Goddess, one should always keep this secret, as one would a mother’s paramour. (70)
Thus ends the eleventh chapter in the glorious Yoginītantra, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The twelfth chapter. The Goddess said:
"O Lord, supreme bliss, bestower of fearlessness upon yogins!"
O Śiva, the greatness of Kāmākhyāyoni which was described by you to me— [1]
This is true, this is true; there is no doubt, for it is entirely wonderful.
In truth, I have realized through its practice that in the Kali age, what does not bestow excellent accomplishment? || 2 ||
We do not see the knowledge of Śiva, nor likewise the accomplishment of mantras;
O Lord, compassionate one, tell me what the cause of this is. (3)
Īśvara said:
"The one named Naraka-asura was born from the seed of Viṣṇu;
produced from the womb of the Earth, he became the supreme lord of the Dānavas."
At the word of the Earth, Viṣṇu granted that Dānava—who was difficult to withstand in battle—a kingdom of great fruit that could assume any form at will. || 5 ||
Having conquered the Kirātas in battle, King Kāma became established there;
and the Blessed One joyfully granted it to him as a dwelling place once again. (6)
Having conquered the famous city of Prāgjyotiṣa, the seat of the womb of Kāmākhyā, Viṣṇu bestowed upon him the consecration in the kingdom as well as his own power.
Then Hari showed him the cave of Manobhava,
and likewise caused Naraka, who had been well-bathed, to be brought there at that time.
Viṣṇu said:
"The entire majesty of Kāmākhyā is in accordance with the meaning of the Vedas;
through her, Brahmā attained the state of Brahmā, and I, moreover, attained the state of Viṣṇu. (9)
And your state of Śiva-hood was attained solely through the grace of Śiva and Kāmākhyā;
therefore, you must worship her, the Yoni, with all your being and with great effort.
When your mother is well-disposed toward you, then your prosperity is stable;
when your mother is averse to you, then there is no good for you, my son.
"At that very moment I shall abandon you; yet I know that you are my son. Knowing this, honor me with special care—what more need I say? (12)
The Lord said: Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu departed for his own abode, Vaikuṇṭha;
Naraka, however, continued to observe whatever vow of Viṣṇu he had undertaken.
In the meantime, O Goddess, hear this terrible account:
Vasiṣṭha, the mind-born son of Brahmā, was exceedingly self-restrained. (14)
Then the sage propitiated Tārā on Mount Nīla;
there, O Goddess, for a single day he worshipped—and indeed chanted—the Mistress of the Gods.
(83) Having arrived at Kāmākhyā-maṇḍala in Purahāra, Naraka chose Tārā, who was born of Brahmā, there as his bride. (16)
Naraka said:
"Stay here now, O Brahmin; do not enter the inner circle.
The Goddess is being worshipped at this moment; you may go once the worship is concluded. (17)
Having heard these words of Naraka, the lord of sages,
who resembled twelve suns, became overwhelmed with rage;
the brahmin Vasiṣṭha, his eyes copper-red, spoke to Naraka.
Vasiṣṭha said:
"O most wicked one, what have you said? O evil-minded one, I am unworthy! At the time of the worship of Kāmākhyā, may we not find [you] within our home. (19)
O fool, though born of Brahmā, you have become deluded regarding entry into another womb;
now behold my great power, which shall bring about your destruction. (20)
Ishvara said:
Having spoken thus, that sage Vashishtha took water with his hand from his water-pot and pronounced a terrible curse upon the Great Goddess.
Vasiṣṭha said:
"O Mother Kāmākhyā, I too am born of Brahmā;
having abandoned you today, I shall depart, and nothing more need be said by you."
"Truly, the sin arising from the murder of a Brahmin shall be yours today.
Furthermore, according to my word, no success shall ever arise here at this great seat (mahāpīṭha) through recitation or even through worship. (23)
Īśvara said:
Having uttered this terrible curse and abandoned that excellent water, he left Nīlācala and went to Mount Khāṇḍava. (24)
Then that supreme Vidyā named Kāmā, adored by the universe, the Goddess consisting of great light, whose form is universal illumination; (25)
The star was burned day and night right there by the splendor of its own limbs;
instantly consumed by that fire, it departed for the palace of Kailāsa.
At that very moment, O Supreme Goddess, the cave of the mind was once again enveloped by masses of great darkness due to separation from Him. (27)
A cry of "Alas! Alas! arose throughout the entire world, and the lord of the Dānavas fainted;
then he beheld that supreme Māyā once more with a dejected countenance.
Having seen her, I questioned Kāmā with great respect: "O Śivā, how have you come here, having abandoned that circle of wombs? (29)
"Having become dejected in countenance, speak the reason for this, O Kāmākhyā!
You, O Goddess, are the supreme one to be worshipped; please abide within my heart yourself. (30)
I shall indeed repay everything; how can I [behave] with such a dejected countenance? 31.
Kāmākhyā said:
"O Lord, the sage Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā, has come to my doorway within the circle of my womb in order to propitiate Tārā. (32)
At dawn, a Brahmin arrived there to worship me; meanwhile, the king became the gatekeeper until my worship was completed.
Indeed, no one at all was able to enter my realm;
thus was it perpetually restricted by the Asura Naraka.
(85) Therefore, Naraka restrained that son of Brahmā;
then, by that very sage, a most terrible curse was pronounced. || 35 ||
O Mahādeva, hear my curse; in speaking thus, I weep.
"O Lord, that supreme state which is desired even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the other gods has been thwarted for me; tell me, what remedy is there for me? (37)
"Leaving you, I shall go to another place today; for if I were to go now otherwise, nothing would be said by you.
Truly, the sin arising from the murder of a Brahmin will be yours today. (38)
Thus, in this great seat (mahāpīṭha), neither through recitation nor even through worship does accomplishment ever arise at any time, contrary to my word. (39)
"In this very way, having come into your presence due to the sage’s curse, what means shall I employ? Tell me, O Compassionate One.
Īśvara said:
Having spoken thus and having consoled her who was weeping again and again,
I returned to the seat of the womb (yonipīṭha) and chanted the mantra of Kālikā.
For the sake of removing the curse, the Goddess was liberated from that curse;
she then re-established Kāmākhyā in the vulva-mandala as it was before.
Then that supreme Māyā attained great joy;
however, O Maheśānī, during the Kali age for three hundred years, the curse of Brahmā will certainly bear fruit, O Maheśānī. (43)
The Goddess said:
"In former times, Kāmākhyā, who dwells in Kāma, was cursed by Vasiṣṭha;
all of that, along with the context of Naraka, has been recounted to me. (44)
(86) Now I wish to hear the story of your release from the curse.
How is the curse to be recognized? Tell me its characteristics as well, so that upon hearing it, all virtuous people will always show compassion.
Īśvara said:
O Supreme Goddess, from the day that the destruction of the kingdom of the foolish King Puru occurs,
the curse of Brahmā comes into effect.
Then, he will become exceedingly wicked in conduct in Kāmarūpa;
causing affliction to the subjects and spreading disease, he will be full of many evils. || 47 ||
O Mahāmāyā, there is constant war and perpetual wickedness;
the gods, dānavas, and gandharvas are always intent on causing affliction.
In the Śaka year measured by the moon (one) preceded by *ku* (nine), that is, 911, there will be a fierce battle day and night between the Somaras and the Yavanas with their wicked speech. (49)
On the back of the Kāma mountain, there will be a place crowded with a vast army;
from there, having conquered the Yavana-king Soma in battle according to his desire, [he shall prevail]. (50)
The king, whose name begins with the letter 'Ma', ruled the kingdom for exactly one year;
having obtained that assistance, he spoke wicked words while enjoying his own sovereignty.
O Maheśvarī, at the end of the rainy season, having conquered the Yavana, Saumāra became the leader of the kingdom when the Śaka year 1642 had passed.
In Kāmarūpa, there will be a union with the back of the jewel [a union for battle (ka) with the jewel];
likewise, O Maheśvarī, there shall be a kingdom in Kāmarūpa for twelve years.
Having become associated with false speech, the Yavana will act;
then, beginning with the fifth letter of the sixth group, he desires a [new] body. (54)
Kāmarūpa is to be subdued by the Saumāras and the Kuvācakas;
likewise, Yavana, Kuvāca, Saumāra, and Plava. || 55 ||
O Goddess, the lord of Kāmarūpa is none other than he even amidst the curse;
O Īśvarī, I shall describe many such various characteristics in this very way.
O Supreme Goddess, O passionate one, a visible act of honoring is performed;
at the beginning of Vasiṣṭha’s ascetic penance, even the fire was extinguished.
And there shall be trees upon the mountain named Śāla—at the gateway to heaven, at the fall of the rock, and in the vicinity of Ekaparvata. (58)
O Goddess of the gods, when the monastery of Kāmākhyā was destroyed, there occurred a union with one resembling Urvaśī;
O Lord of the gods, the subtle stream belongs to that son of Brahmā.

When sixteen years of the Śaka era have passed, and when the earth is like a mere speck for the enemy of the earth (Viṣṇu), the conjunction of Saumya (Mercury), Arka (the Sun), Kāma (Venus), and Pṛṣṭhya (Saturn) will surely come to pass.
Having worshipped there for six months during both the northern and southern courses of the sun,
all those kings who are skilled in warfare will depart.
A great battle will take place, crowded with many troops consisting of Kuvācas, Yavanas, and Aindras, and filled with three Mlecchas.
Especially with horse-heads, human heads, and elephant heads, the Lohitya river will undoubtedly become filled with blood. || 63 ||
At that very moment, the supreme Māyā, adored by the host of Yoginīs,
appeared as Kāmākhyā— dark-hued as collyrium, holding an offering in her hand, and with a smiling face.
With a flickering tongue, wearing a garland of severed heads and clad in the directions as her garment, she stands supreme;
having taken refuge on a mountain peak, she will drink blood. (65)
Then, abandoning the Yavana after he had been destroyed by Saumya,
Kuvāca will wage a great battle as far as the Karatoyā river.
Having remained there for ten days, he will return again to his own abode;
thereafter, that brahmin, having become a king, will dwell in Kāmarūpa.
"O Goddess, he will make the people devoted to recitation, worship, and other such practices.
Having ruled the kingdom in this manner for three years, King Daṇḍin, the twice-born, [will depart]. (68)
O Mahāmāyā, it will come to be in the vicinity of the womb-maṇḍala;
from there, the navel with its twelve petals is fashioned as the king of the previous ground. (69)
Having arrived from the northeast (or having come to the northeast), he shall bring all desires under a single umbrella;
O Goddess, he will protect that entire kingdom with righteousness.
His wife shall be dark-complexioned; that virtuous woman shall have propitiated Pārvatī.
She shall have a son who is a king, and a daughter who is a princess. (71)
O Goddess, from the day of his birth until the twelfth day,
the touch-stone (sparśamaṇi) shall manifest on Mount Sparśācala.
By that very [means], all the wealthy inhabitants of Kāmarūpa shall become [prosperous],
and at that very time there shall be liberation from the curse of Vasiṣṭha.
Then, in the Kali age, there will be abundant splendors within the yoni-maṇḍala of Kāmākhyā and in the presence of Kāmākhyā.
And at that very moment, O Goddess, there shall be the accomplishment of mantras within the Yoni-maṇḍala; for Kāmākhyā will indeed bestow the fruits as described.
Due to the curse of Brahmā, which rendered her inert, for three hundred years Kāmākhyā herself felt ashamed, even though her lotus feet are worshipped by the gods. (76)
O Goddess, everything will then come to pass as before;
thus, the protection from desire has been briefly told by me. O Girijā, what more is to be heard? Let it be told by you.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The thirteenth chapter.
The Goddess said: O Lord of Gods, O Supreme Ruler, O Omniscient One, O You who are worshipped by all!
O Protector, O Śaṅkara, tell me out of compassion: where are you going so frequently? 1.
Īśvara said: In the region known as Koñcāna, near Yonigarta, there was a virtuous and chaste woman named Revatī, renowned among the people [though now forgotten by them]. || 2 ||
The Yoginī who is born from the body of a Mleccha is considered to be Sundarī;
her breasts are firm and paired, and she possesses fullness in the region of the womb.
O Great Goddess, as I wander day and night on my rounds for alms, I find great delight in her presence.
The Goddess said:
Where were you? What austerity was performed? How did you reach the surface of the earth?
For she whose delight is with you is not the fruit of meager penance. (5)
Nevertheless, great compassion for her is observed by me;
tell me now, what has happened, for she is possessed of supreme compassion? (6)
Īśvara said:
"O daughter of the mountain king, O young girl, O beloved of my life, listen;
O lady of pure smiles, I shall relate to you a portion of that virtuous woman's conduct."
In the forest of Ekāmra, she joyfully engaged in the play of rasa with him;
that virtuous Yoginī, born from the Vedāṅgas, is considered a goddess. (8)
O daughter of the mountain, there was indeed no complete satisfaction for her in my ritual service;
she remained intensely longing and tormented by the desire to attain me in this field that grants all wishes.
O Goddess, in the dense forest of Ekāmra on that mountain crowded with sacred fords,
a certain brahmin went there for the sake of alms and spoke to her.
"No answer was given to her; let alone alms, she was kept at a distance.
Then the brahmin cursed her: 'O arrogant woman, go to the state of a barbarian!'"
Having spoken thus, that brahmin departed, and the Yoginī attained the state of a Mleccha.
Therefore, O Goddess, if I am capable and yet do not give what is requested by one who seeks it, may I always become his slave, purchased by his ascetic merit.
Therefore, my beloved wife has always been devoted to him;
his son, Vinuṣiṃha, was born from my own loins.
(91) By himself, that glorious and high-minded one conquered the Kāmās, the Saumārās, and the Gauḍapañcamas; having utterly defeated all those kings, he alone remained triumphant. || 15 ||
He too had many sons who were protectors of the earth;
all those kings were righteous, yet fierce in battle, and possessed of eloquent speech. (16)

O Mother, having resorted to yoga, that Viṣṇu-siṃha remains in an unmanifest form upon the throne until the end of the kalpa, in order to perform penance [in such a state] while the world is distracted and desolate.
In the course of time, that goddess Mādhavī entered into my body and became lowly;
just as she was the wife of Nandimitra, so too is she considered a yoginī.
Just as Bhṛṅgarīṭa was my son, so too is Vinu my offspring;
Vinusiṃha also shall attain supreme perfection at the end of the kalpa.
All the kings born of that lineage shall be dwellers of Kailāsa;
they will be high-souled lords of the Gaṇas (or lords of wealth), endowed with every excellence.
O Goddess, they always sport and play like Bhairavas together with hosts of celestial maidens endowed with beauty and youth.
Whenever the curse of the Brahmins should again fall upon Kāmākhyā,
he descends at each such time as the protector of his own desire.
Likewise, O Goddess of the Gods, all those born of that lineage shall be guardians of desire (Kāmapālakas) for the duration of a kalpa, until the curse is released.
O Mahāmāyā, O Great Goddess, he certainly sports with that power for as long as a kalpa, which in the Kali age is three hundred years. (24)
O Supreme Goddess, for years she who is of the nature of Parā experiences the curse of worldly enjoyment;
but at the end of that, O Mahāmāyā, Kāmākhyā shall become everything.
(92) Thus, O Goddess, Maheśānī, I have certainly explained in its entirety the liberation from the curse of Brahmā regarding Kāmākhyā. 26.
For one upon whom a Brahmin’s curse has fallen, there is no remedy even from afar;
yet for one bitten by Takṣaka, a remedy exists at that very moment.
For one who has incurred the curse of a Brahmin, there may be a remedy at the end of a kalpa;
but for that [sin], there is no atonement from hell, because of its very nature—of this there is no doubt. (28)
In this way, O beloved, all those born of that lineage are tormented day and night by various kinds of great portents for as long as seven generations.
Therefore, O Goddess, one should never despise a Brāhmaṇa anywhere;
for the Brāhmaṇa embodies all the gods and is the very essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
A twice-born man who is always naturally endowed with the splendor of Brahman—
wherever he eats while being served by Brāhmaṇas, there Hari himself eats.
There, Brahmā, Rudra, the sky-faring sages, the munis, the ancestors, and all the deities partake [of the offerings]; of this there is no doubt. (32)
A Brahmin embodies all the gods; therefore, do not despise him. Nor should one despise a Brahmin, a young girl, a spear, fire, the Veda, or a cow. (33)
Those gods always desire [a maiden] for the sake of worship in the lands of action;
if one maiden has been worshipped, there may be a second worship. (34)
I am unable to describe the fruit of worshipping a maiden;
for maidens are Śaktis, and all this world, both moving and unmoving, is they. (35)
If even one young goddess is worshipped and perceived as one's own self, then all the supreme goddesses are undoubtedly worshipped. (36)
An offering made into the fire yields a single-fold merit, and what is given to a twice-born man yields a single-fold merit;
however, through trust, it is obtained multiplied ten millionfold—of this there is no doubt. (37)
In this world, the fruit of non-belief is certainly a hundredfold; however, the offering of a morsel of food to a cow is purifying and destroys all sins. (38)

O Maheśvarī, that which is given by maidens and likewise by Śaktis never perishes at any time, even after hundreds of millions of kalpas; indeed, for them, it lasts for tens of thousands of millions of kalpas. (39)
For the gods have Dharma as their source; Dharma is considered to be the sacrifice and so forth.
Dharma is a great kinsman in the next world; there is no doubt about this. || 40 ||
O Goddess, having performed only Vedic rites throughout many births,
he then proceeds by means of dharma alone toward the dharma revealed in the Āgamas.
There, liberation that destroys the bondage of karma is attained;
thereafter, at the end of many births, having acquired knowledge, one is released.
Through action one obtains devotion; through devotion one attains knowledge;
from knowledge comes liberation, O Great Goddess—this truth, this very truth, I declare. (43)
"When the absence of knowledge has arisen, having attained the one who desires knowledge [the supreme knowledge], then the yogi shall be liberated; thus spoke the Blessed Lord Śiva. (44)
A person does not attain freedom from action by abstaining from the undertaking of action;
therefore, O Great Illusion, one should always perform action.
Whether it be Vedic or Tantric, if one has obtained [this knowledge] through good fortune, a wise person should not let time pass in vain through gambling, games, and the like. (46)
One should cause [the disciple] to proceed by means of deity worship, recitation, sacrifice, hymns, and so forth;
for that ritual action is indeed twofold, distinguished as external and internal. (47)
The external [mind] is attached to what is unrestricted, whereas the mental [mind] is not so; whether it be impure or pure, it remains as it is in whatever place. (48)
Whether walking, standing, or even sleeping, O fair-faced one, whatever mental dharma one may perform, there is never any fault in what is mental.
O Maheśvarī, among all actions, the knowledge of recitation (japa) is the most excellent;
O Maheśānī, the sacrifice of recitation is my own very form, without a doubt. (50)
O Supreme Goddess, he who remains established in the sacrifice of recitation (japayajña), whether externally or internally, is at all times liberated while living; of this there is no doubt.
O Maheśvarī, whatever Vedic and Tantric dharmas exist,
none of them are worth even a sixteenth part of the sacrifice of japa.
O Goddess, the planets, spirits, and piśācas, as well as the hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas, and creatures such as tigers, who are likewise inwardly provoked; (53)
The ḍākinīs and the guhyakas, the gandharvas and the reptiles, the dānavas, the bhairavas, and those who are wicked dwellers of the cremation grounds. || 54 ||
O Goddess, some, overwhelmed by fear, do not even look at that practitioner who recites the mantra;
nor, O Beloved, do sins ever touch the adept.
This fruit has been proclaimed for vocal recitation;
the whispered recitation (upāṃśu) shall be a hundredfold, and the mental (mānasa) is considered a thousandfold.
One should utter the mantra with the voice; this is declared to be vocal recitation (vācika-japa).
That which is accompanied by slight audible sound is proclaimed as whispered recitation (upāṃśu). || 57 ||
That which is beyond the range of one's own ears is proclaimed to be mental;
whereas vocal recitation is external, since mental recitation is internal. (58)
The whispered [japa] is indeed mixed; this threefold recitation is thus remembered.
By means of japa, the deity, being constantly praised, becomes propitious. (59)
When pleased, she bestows abundant desires and eternal liberation;
O fair-faced one, [she grants] the means of accomplishment, the recitation, and meditation as well. (60)
O Goddess, it is not obtained by anyone anywhere through slight austerity;
rather, O Queen of Gods, it is attained only through fortune accumulated over many births.
If that which is attained there results in liberation through even a single birth, and that which is called the knowledge of Brahman is proclaimed as *samādhi*. (62)
Thus has this delightful account been told in brief, O Maheśvarī.
Beyond this, O Mahādevī, what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the *Śrīyoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Lord of Goddesses.
[Now begins] the fourteenth chapter.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, O God of supreme bliss, O Great Lord of Yoga!
I desire to hear; O God, O Guru, please tell me out of compassion what and where it is.
I have heard the account of the Brahmin and of your eternal semen.
Plava, Yavana, Saumāra, and Maheśvara. || 2 ||
(96) From their semen were born those Mlecchas who are the guardians of desire. O Mahādeva, compassionate one, tell me how they were born. (3)
Īśvara said:
"O Three-eyed One, the sons of Śālva and the Bāhlīkas have died in the battle of the Kauravas; there is no other bearer of their lineage remaining in that dynasty."
At that time, there was Kīrti, the beloved of the Vāhlīkas—virtuous, auspicious, youthful, beautiful, charming, devoted to asceticism, and highly intelligent. (5)
Having gone to Kāśī at the desire of her son, she performed austerities day and night,
staying before Viśveśvara in my gateway, the Muktimaṇḍapa.
Then, O Goddess, Bāṇa, the son of Bali, who was Mahākāla and possessed of great strength,
who served as the gatekeeper there, became agitated upon beholding her.
Taking up his office, Bhairava, deluded by passion,
wearing a garland of skulls and possessing a drunken, intoxicated appearance, was exhilarated by the fragrance of wine.
Assuming the guise of an ascetic, the shameless Lord of Pleasure appeared,
O Great Goddess, with the luster of a Bandhūka flower or an Āmalaka fruit.
