There, O Great Goddess, Bhairava Vipula was born; from him was born Mahāṅkuśa, the son of Kīrti, from the seed of Mahākāla.
Seeing his affection there, I became the son of that Bhairava; and she [bestowed] constant delight upon me, whose great arms were like mighty goads.
O Śāmbhavī, [the Lord] granted him the attainment of a kingdom along with fame and power;
having given the kingdom of Śālva to Mahāṅkuśa, [Śālva, the son of Kāmarūpa, attained the kingdom as Mahāṅkuśa].
Having attained the source of fame, one who is devoted to the conduct of his lineage should always worship there just as he does in Kāśī. (13)
There, a great worship shall take place day and night.
O Mahāṅkuśa, having arisen, how could there be an assault upon Kāśī?
Then the one named Plaveti went to the Maṇimaṇḍapa.
Thus, O Goddess, has this account concerning the Plava [manvantara] been narrated to you. || 15 ||
I shall relate a certain account of the Yavanas; listen to that.
In the Tretā age, there was a king who was devoted to many forms of dharma. (16)
The great sovereign and mighty warrior, born of the solar dynasty,
having utterly defeated his father’s enemies, [ruled] the earth with its seven islands.
For a long time, O Mahāmāyā, he enjoyed supreme desire and extensive yoga-meditation; thereafter, he was deluded by his own pride.
There has never been a king superior to me on this earth;
for I have struck down the enemies of my father and performed the ancestral śrāddha rites for him.
Thus, having given rise to self-conceit (ahaṅkāra), he indeed brought about the destruction of everything;
therefore, O mighty-armed one, a flow of sin arose within him.
A king who is evil-minded should never exercise sovereignty;
he should always practice ego-restraint and never lack self-discipline.
All these great sins, along with their constituent parts, were certainly present in him;
by that very state of being, his royal fortune fell away.
The Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas, those best of kings, having appeared and consulted together, then crossed the ocean. (23)
Under the pretext of paying tribute, they attained superior skill;
at first, Bāhu was defeated by them, emerging [from the contest] after a month.
Having lost his kingdom and with his arm severed, Bāhu went to the forest accompanied by his wife;
in that forest, Bāhu died, and at that time everything became devoid of luster.
By him, the two kings—the Tālajaṅghas and the Haihayas—were utterly defeated;
then, at the conclusion of Vasiṣṭha’s life, they both went to his hermitage, for such was their destiny.
Furthermore, those two kings were as breathless as the winds themselves.
They sought refuge with Vasiṣṭha, crying out, "Protect us! Protect us! || 27 ||
Then the brahmin Vasiṣṭha granted freedom from fear to those Yavanas.
In the meantime, O King, Sagara raised his sword in a fit of rage.
Desiring to slay those kings, he went into the presence of Vasiṣṭha;
and seeing the king in that state, Vasiṣṭha, who was born of Brahmā, [spoke].
She said to Sagara, the knower of dharma and son of Bāhu:
"O son of Bāhu, do not cause harm; I have granted you fearlessness."
Hearing that, the king was startled: "He will be a Kṣatriya and a man of action;
the word of Brahmā must not be in vain, nor shall my own promise to my ancestors be broken. (31)
"What shall I do now? A crisis has arisen.
Having reflected thus, he reported all of that to Vasiṣṭha. (32)
"I shall slay the hosts of men; this was the vow I made long ago.
Having heard those words, I went there; what am I to do now? (33)
O Sage, I never spoke at that time in order to alter those words;
for if you do not employ a remedy, then death is better for us.
Having heard this, Vasiṣṭha quickly replied.
Vasiṣṭha said:
"Do not fall into despair, my friend; hear from me what must be done. Having shaved the heads of all these enemies of yours,"
He caused those who had strayed outside the Vedic conduct to be banished to a distance.
"On the western side of the Himalaya mountain, there is a land where a Yavana king resides;
thus shall my word remain, O Lord, as well as your own vow, O Child. (37)
For the shaving of the head is indeed like the cutting off of the head;
even in the Veda, this is declared to be equally constant. (38)
Īśvara said: Having heard those words, Sagara likewise acted accordingly;
and all those Kṣatriyas—the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghakas—did so as well. (39)
Deprived [of their status], they were always mocked, with their heads shaven;
yet, by taking refuge in the sage Suṣeṇa, they became resplendent through his conduct.
Following the instruction of Suṣeṇa, they performed penance, having taken refuge in him;
O Great Goddess, it was by relying on him that those devoted to the practices of the Mlecchas [attained their goal]. 41.
O Great Goddess, they are of the nature of *tamas*, having resorted to a state of *tamas*;
for mantras there is a twofold course: conjunction and disjunction. (42)
O Goddess, the union of the *sāttvika* and *rājasa* natures bestows fruit;
indeed, through the separation of the external and internal, that union is unsurpassed. (43)
In the tamasic [path], however, there is external disjunction which bestows the fruit of supernatural powers;
the tamasic external dharma is the Lord of the other world.
Because of that very disposition of theirs, faith arises within me;
I have granted them a boon—listen as they wish for their boon.
"O Yavana, enjoy this kingdom now and remain here, until eight hundred and ninety years of the Śaka era have passed in the Kali age. (46)
"You shall certainly become sovereigns of meritorious lands;
even so, O Maheśānī, O Śivā, you shall be sovereigns of Kāmarūpa."
By my grace, as well as through other merits, that Yavana shall joyfully enjoy the earth in the Kali age, filled with many kings. || 48 ||
Thus has this ever-purifying account been told to you, O Goddess;
now listen likewise to the deeds of Saumāraka in battle.
Once, the King of the Dead (Yama), having been seized by his enemies, came to the Khāṇḍava forest;
leaving behind the sovereignty of the gods and the King of the Gods himself, he went there accompanied by Kauśāṅgī. || 50 ||
After much time had passed in play, the king of the gods developed a thorough desire for the threefold symphony (tauryatrika) and likewise for many other [diversions]. (51)
Having summoned Rambhā, Tilottamā, Kāñcī, Kuraṅgākṣī, and Manoharā, he commanded them to perform a dance with Rambhā. (52)
Then all those courtesans, surrounded by him, departed filled with joy;
and Mohinī, through various kinds of ritual performances, gratified Indra.
And Kauśāṅgī, being infatuated, was united with the King of the Gods;
then, by their dancing and singing, the fire of passion was kindled. [There will be a fall from desire.
In this interval, O Goddess, the celestial courtesan Manoharā—
With her, the Lord of the Gods, the slayer of Bala, that king of joyful mind, made love.
Having beheld Indra in such a state, Kauśāṅgī likewise set her heart upon him.
Distraught by the fires of desire and stumbling amidst the dances and songs of the Kāmarūpas, Rati’s fortitude was shaken; yet, when she stumbled, his [fortitude] arose once more.
Then, having understood her mind, Kauśāṅgī, overcome with anger, spoke these harsh words: "Listen, O charming lady, O Goddess! (58)
Having become a courtesan, greatly wicked and with a mind distracted by intoxication, you desire the god who is my beloved;
therefore, our minds have been set in motion toward this transgressive act.
"Alas! Go to the earth, O courtesan, and obtain a king as your husband!
Thus was this wicked curse uttered, issuing from the mouth of Kauśāṅgī.
Having heard this, Kauśāṅgī fainted and fell at his feet;
holding his feet repeatedly, she lamented in many ways. (61)
Then Kauśāṅgī spoke: "O Manoharā, having experienced this curse on earth for thirty-two years, you shall again go to heaven with full splendor and happiness. (62)
Having cast off her body in the Mandākinī, she was thereafter born among humans as the lovely and enchanting Kaṅkatī, who went to Dhārtarāṣṭra as her husband.
When the Kaurava was slain at Kurukṣetra, a hundred women died;
and out of fear, Kaṅkatī quickly went to the Moon-crested Mountain.
On its exceedingly high peak she stood, deeply distressed;
having reached her season, that celestial courtesan [remained] on the second day in that direction.
Constantly pierced by the arrows of desire, she fainted and fell into a state of torment;
then, having mounted his chariot, Indra went forth and beheld Sundarī as she sat upon her own chariot. || 66 ||
Having remembered her from Kuśadvīpa with all her ornaments, and having awakened that beloved woman who was utterly deluded by passion, he explained to her the entire cause of their previous lives.
Having conceived a passion for her and taken her as his wife, O Supreme Goddess, a son was born to Kaṅkatī on Mount Gandhamādana; he was Ariṃdama.
Since Indra took her on the second day during her season,
he thereafter became known as Arindama and was devoted to the customs of the Mlecchas.
Therefore, O Goddess, he followed the terrible livelihood of a hunter, always harming living beings; he was a consumer of all kinds of meat, like a Kirāta who had been fashioned for such a purpose.
Excluded from all merit, filled with every kind of evil, consuming liquor, meat, and excrement, he is devoted to the most depraved conduct. (71)
Seeing her son in such a state, Kaṅkatī was deeply afflicted with grief;
she performed most intense penance for the sake of the fourfold essence, the essence of essences, the supreme beyond the supreme.
Then that King of the Gods, standing before her, spoke to her.
Indra said:
"Tell me, how was such terrible penance performed by you? I am highly pleased with your asceticism; tell me what you desire and I shall grant it."
Kaṅkatī said:
"O Lord of Gods, such a son has been born to you, one who is always devoted to sin; I am not able to look upon him—do as you wish. (74)
O God of gods, Lord of gods, O Sovereign of the Suras, let this son of yours be true—of this there is no doubt—but let that lowest of men be a son [to me]. (75)
Therefore, O Lord of the gods, you are his father and he is your son;
do as you wish, but lead me away quickly, O Master. (76)
Appoint me as a handmaid in your service by your side;
O Lord of Gods, he alone is desirable, never anyone else.
Indra said:
"Listen, my beloved, to my words; the time for your curse has passed.
I shall take you away now with haste; remain steadfast."
Due to the son's connection with sin, he became the cause of the destruction of the lineage;
therefore, when the one hundred and twenty-eighth person has been lost, || 79 ||
(104) My ancestors, those preeminent kings, were inhabitants of Saurāṣṭra;
they were of meritorious fame, composed of dharma, and devoted to righteous conduct. (80)
Possessing logical intellect and great enthusiasm, devoted to the gods and the Brahmins, they will once again become knowers of the reality of Brahman; of this there is no doubt.
They shall all go to Vaikuṇṭha and become beloved of Viṣṇu;
they will remain there until the final dissolution of all beings (ābhūtasaṃplava).
Īśvara said:
Then, taking her with him, Indra went to his own abode;
meanwhile, in due time, Saumārī became the lord of Kāmarūpa.
In the eastern region is Saumāra, and likewise Kuvāca in the west;
in the south is Yavana, and similarly Plava in the north.
Thus, O Great Goddess, all of them are the guardians of desire.
Thus, O Goddess, has that history of Saumāraka been narrated to you.
"What do you wish to hear from here that has not yet been heard by you?
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The Fifteenth Chapter. The Goddess said:
"I ask you in secret; tell me, what is Kāmākhyā?"
Īśvara said:
O Goddess of gods, that which is Kālī—the supreme knowledge, eternal, and of the nature of Brahman—is indeed Kāmākhyā, the bestower of all accomplishments. (2)
The Goddess said: O Maheśvara, how did Kālī, who is the form of Brahman, become Kāmākhyā?
O Lord, O Moon-crested One, tell me everything out of compassion.
Ishvara said:
When the creation was performed by the Self-born Creator himself,
that Grandfather (Brahmā) became filled with the defect of egoism.
"O Īśvarī, egoism (ahaṅkāra) brings about the destruction of everything; it is the destroyer of all for everyone, O Īśvarī.
Taking up that egoism, Brahmā, the storehouse of the world, remained [established]. || 5 ||
Having forgotten all that was previously said by Kālikā,
he was indeed always possessed of mere egoism by the Creator.
The universe, which is the abode of all desires and consists of desire, belongs to whom, or by what could it have been made?
Nevertheless, O Goddess, Brahmā is delighted by the ego-sense born of illusion (māyā).
O Supreme Goddess, O Śivā, having beheld Brahmā in such a state,
[the Lord] fashioned him from that body and from his ego-sense (ahaṅkāra).
Having emerged from the body of Brahmā, there appeared an exceedingly fierce Daitya named Keśin, the most difficult to subdue and supreme. 9.
Then, O Goddess, she ran there to devour Brahmā;
consequently, the Grandfather fled along with Viṣṇu.
Then the great Daitya Keśin built a city in Bhārata;
this is known as Keśipura, for the Dānava resided there. (11)

O Goddess, by the mere chanting of the word "Brahman"— [the sound "Kill Brahmā"]— he consumed the entire realm of Bhūr, Bhuvas, and Svar, including all moving and non-moving beings, throughout the circle of the universe at all times. 12.
Then Brahmā, the sustainer of the world, rendered free from ego by Viṣṇu,
praised Kālī, the mother and sustainer of the worlds, who destroys all obstacles.
Brahmā and Viṣṇu said:
"Salutations to the Supreme Auspicious One, the Sovereign whose essence is the Praṇava, who is the very nature of her own seed-syllable and the embodiment of the Kāma-bīja. (14)
She is beautiful with a garland of severed heads, possessing a lolling tongue, eternal,
having the nature of the seed-syllable of Māyā, and having the nature of the Kūrca-bīja.
I bow to Kālī, the mother of the worlds, whose eyes are like lotuses, who utters a terrible roar, who is united with Śiva, and who has disheveled hair and is naked. 16.
I bow to Mother Kālikā, the destroyer of great obstacles;
I perpetually prostrate before that beloved Mother, the Sovereign of the World.
The Lord said: Thus praised then by Brahmā and by Viṣṇu as well, a voice from the sky suddenly spoke: "O Grandfather, what do you desire?"
O Viṣṇu, O mighty-armed one, tell me what it is that you desire.
Brahmā and Viṣṇu said:
"A single preeminent Daitya has been born, a great Asura named Keśin;
by him our entire realm has been constantly carried off and seized. (19)
(p. 107) "Now that you have slain that asura, establish us both as before.
Grant us servitude at your lotus feet; let that be our greatness. (20)
Kālī said:
Listen, O Brahmin, to these words; indeed, your ego has departed.
Now you have attained full realization, and those who are superior to you are passing away.
The entire universe consists of illusion; however, upon seeing another’s pride regarding the lotus, an insurmountable obstacle was placed [before him]. (22)
O Sustainer of the World, I shall indeed slay that one who has assumed the form of the Daitya Keśi—him whom I have fashioned from your own ego; therefore, remain steadfast.
Do not fear, O Viṣṇu; remain steadfast, O high-minded one.
The Lord said: Having thus approached and consoled her, she who is essentially identical with Brahmā, Viṣṇu,
and the Supreme Self, reduced that foremost of Dānavas to ashes by a mere *huṃ* sound.
Then Kālī spoke these words to the great asura Keśin regarding the ritual procedure.
Kālī said: "O Brahman, from your egoism has arisen a most great sin;
for the removal of that sin, this best of mountains is being fashioned. (26)
Moreover, you have long held the cow's fodder along with the ashes of the Daitya Keśi;
by the constant use of the ashes from that fodder, your sin shall be destroyed. (27)
Īśvara said:
Having unified that ash produced from the body of the Daitya Keśin,
Brahmā fashioned a mountain by pouring water from his water-pot.
A morsel of grass held out for a cow, neither too high nor too low, should be grasped with many [fingers].
By the ashes of that morsel, the cow will certainly attain satisfaction and nourishment. (29)
Therefore, Brahmā gave the name Govardhana to that mountain;
and according to the sacred tradition, the cow ate her fodder upon that best of mountains.
In that same measure, O Śivā, the sin of a Brāhmaṇa goes to destruction;
indeed, the expiation for the Creator lasts only as long as Mount Govardhana remains.
At its conclusion, O Supreme Goddess, there is atonement for that offense against Brahman;
such indeed is the case even if your own offense occurs through negligence.
O Three-eyed One, that fruit is the affliction for him and for all;
therefore, Brahmā, the sustainer of the world, and Viṣṇu, the lord of the worlds, [are affected]. (33)
And again, he praised the Supreme Goddess in that very same sequence.
Then Kālī, the Mother of the World, said to them, "What do you desire?"
"I give all that to you two, my children; why are you both so despondent? (34)
Brahmā and Viṣṇu said:
"Fallen from Your feet for the welfare of ourselves and the worlds, it is exceedingly pure and bestows great liberation. (35)
"O Mother, how shall we worship that which is invisible, hidden, and devoid of form, yet bestows all auspiciousness? (36)
Prepare a place upon the ground to chant the prayer to your lotus feet;
we two shall always worship that which is the cause of great auspiciousness.
And for both of us, as well as for all others, it is for the sake of the fruit of great liberation;
therefore, what can the Dānavas and other inauspicious beings do to us? (38)
(109) We two shall certainly cross over [this world] which is difficult to cross, through the worship of your feet. || 39 ||
Kālī said:
"Listen, O child Mahāviṣṇu, to these most supreme and great words: by means of which seed-syllable of the *huṅkāra* of water, he reduced the Dānava to ashes. (40)
Know that the Keśī-mantra, the great seed-syllable, whose nature is the Sound-Brahman (Śabdabrahman), consists of great splendor; that seed-syllable is the supreme state.
And in Keśipura, that seed was established by the slayer of Keśin;
extending as far as the netherworld (Pātāla), that seed was enveloped in splendor for the distance of one krośa.
Therefore, that place is certainly worthy of worship, being composed of great splendor;
taking hold of that place, worship me as you desire. (43)
O Great-minded One, even by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, and others, the desired fruit is obtained through a state of extreme secrecy. (44)
Perform my worship in such a way that no one knows of it;
I shall always protect you from all calamities.
"This place of sport has always been described to you by me as belonging to Viṣṇu;
indeed, the power of will was granted to him by me in the beginning. (46)
Abiding in Brahman, she serves in the form of Mahālakṣmī;
she herself will manifest here in this city in the form of Vṛndā.
Then, having pervaded Keśipura and the place named Vṛndāvana,
your sporting with her will certainly take place in Keśipura.
Having become a tree in Vṛndāvana, she will remain there forever as Lakṣmī;
for she shall be the destroyer of all demons, removing the obstacles posed by the Daityas.
O Brahmin, my child, listen to these words of mine which bring about auspicious results, concerning how your worship was performed for the sake of slaying the Daitya Keśin. (50)
"O you two, behold there my vulva-circle that has been produced;
know that this vulva-circle has arisen from my own splendor."
The womb alone is the place of origin for all beings, without a doubt;
O God, know that my own Prakṛti is my womb. 52.
"O Lord of Gods, having worshipped the Yoni, perform creation according to the truth;
O Grandfather, may there be no fear for you anywhere at all. (53)
I have a presiding presence in that sacred seat (pīṭha), of this there is no doubt;
know that my form as its presiding deity is exceedingly beautiful. (54)
Constantly worship that form in the yoni-maṇḍala known as Kāmākhyā.
Whoever, having reached the yoni-maṇḍala, worships Kāmākhyā— || 55 ||
Having become the lord of all accomplishments, he rejoices both in this world and the next;
for him, no fear arises from anywhere or from anyone whatsoever. (56)
For the sake of the welfare of yourself and others, the Yonimaṇḍala has been established on earth in the land of Bhārata, as the great abode of Kāmarūpa. (57)
It is filled with nine wombs and bestows the fruit of great liberation;
O Brahman, it is composed of nine wombs, takes any form at will, and is enchanting to the mind. (58)
O Lord, the circle of the womb blazes with the splendor of Kāmākhyā;
however, I do not perceive your sin in any way whatsoever. (59)
From egoism (ahaṅkāra) has arisen your threefold sin—namely, that of the body, that of speech, and likewise that of the mind. (60)
(111) Because of that sin, you never perceive my *yonipīṭha*;
it has become bound day and night by streams of sinful contemplation. 61.
In that regard, the verbal sin is manifested from Govardhana;
I shall describe the pacification of those three—listen to me.
Having cast down one of the stars from the world of the stars, O Lord, attain preeminence here; having seen this seat, perform penance.
As long as the light of the Rākṣasī remains merged within the splendor of the womb, so long perform severe penance; at its conclusion, the two sins [shall be removed].
It will be pacified, there is no doubt; take up residence there quickly.
Due to the power of asceticism, it cannot be seen by anyone there. (65)
Indeed, such a destiny shall come to one who is superior through his offenses;
for by establishing the constellations there,
O child, that station shall be proclaimed eternally throughout all the worlds as distinct among the various castes.
The Lord said: Having spoken thus, she who is the Supreme Self, stationed in the sky, fell silent;
then Brahmā and Viṣṇu bowed down to that most auspicious Kālī.
With their minds filled with wonder, the two of them ruled that kingdom.
Thus has been told this secret, which was asked by you, O daughter of the mountain; for this ancient account is indeed highly confidential, O mistress of the lineage. (68)
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The sixteenth chapter. The Goddess said:
"I have indeed heard the ancient account, which was beyond the reach of all others."
Now I wish to hear how she becomes the form of Kālī.
The Lord said: Listen, O Goddess, to this supreme secret, which is beyond the reach of Brahmā and the other gods;
it is the most essential of essentials, O Goddess, and bestows both devotion and liberation.
Once, while Brahmā and Viṣṇu were contending with one another in the ocean of waters, each said, "I am the Lord; I am the Lord."
O Maheśānī, for the sake of their pacification, my supreme and purifying great liṅga, which is immeasurable, manifested within the ocean of waters.
In the midst of that divine [form], which consisted of both knowledge and ignorance, was difficult to behold, and terrifying,
I wandered in the form of Rudra, mounted upon my bull.
Having seen that marvel, their bodies trembling with fear, they praised me with various hymns and spoke to me once again. (6)
Brahmā and Viṣṇu said:
"Tell us, who are you, O one of terrifying form, who have arisen in the ocean of waters?"
Rudrarūpa said:
"Seeing you two contending with one another in the ocean of waters,
I arose in order to test your lordship."
Having heard what was thus uttered, Brahmā and Keśava were struck silent;
realizing that he was meditating in secret, Mādhava became satisfied. (9)
With an agitated mind, Brahmā attained my true nature after meditating;
having realized me solely in the form of Rudra, that lotus-seated one [perceived me].
Becoming overcome with doubt, Brahmā then spoke to Viṣṇu.
Brahmā said:
"O Viṣṇu, this Rudra who has been born from my skull is also considered by me [to be my son]."
The Lord said: Having spoken thus and having uttered mockery— which was censured and condemned by the Creator—
he, O Goddess, created many kinds of most terrible obstacles.
By me, having become an Asura, that obstacle was created for that Brahmā at the time of midday, fashioned in a contemptible manner like the sun.
O Śivā, O Maheśvarī, that Dānava was born from the body under the name Tripura; he carried away everything belonging to all, including Indra and the other gods.
O Goddess of the gods, that Daitya then forcibly seized from Viṣṇu that entire world, as well as everything else except for Garuḍa and Lakṣmī.
The lotus-seat of Brahmā was seized by that very Daitya;
consequently, the gods, led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, fled away.
Having reached the Himālaya, Viṣṇu then spoke to Brahmā.
Viṣṇu said:
"O Creator, Śiva was previously reviled by you in the ocean of waters;
because of that very offense, we have all been tormented. (18)
(114) Then, on this mountain, I shall once again praise the Supreme Lord;
at that very moment, I obtained auspiciousness, which now pleases my heart even more. 19.
Īśvara said:
"Then the gods, led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, performed penance taking refuge on the Himālaya; at that time, my grace was bestowed upon them."
Having made the earth his chariot and the moon and sun his two wheels, having made Brahmā his charioteer and likewise the Vedas his reins; 21.
Having made the gods the wheels of his chariot and the horses themselves the chariots,
and having made Mount Sumeru his bow and Vāsuki his bowstring— 22.

Having made the entire universe, including all that is moving and unmoving, situated upon his chariot, and having appointed Viṣṇu as his arrow, he reduced Tripura to ashes along with all its mobile and immobile beings,
including the gods, demons, and others.
Thereupon, O Great Goddess, I again brought about creation there;
O Goddess, it was there that this entire world of moving and non-moving beings was turned to ashes.
Know that the great cremation ground is the cause of the dissolution of all things;
there, the splendor of all the deceased gods is established. (25)

Having likewise become five *krośas* in extent, he then created through his power of illusion (*māyā*) a body for the Triple City (*traipura*) out of the energy of the worlds, and placed it upon his chest.
There, under the guise of death, I praised the Supreme Goddess;
within that splendor of Mahākālī was the Supreme One, whose form is pure consciousness.
Then that supreme power, Kālī, manifested within that splendor;
indeed, the departure of the splendor toward the great lamp is celebrated as Kālī. (28)
Only the face of Mahākālī was seen within her splendor;
therefore, it is celebrated by the sages as "Girimukha" (The Mountain Face). || 29 ||
O Supreme Goddess, upon seeing that, bliss indeed arises;
therefore, it is sung of by the exponents of the Vedas as Ānandakānana (the Forest of Bliss). || 30 ||
Indeed, that entire splendor became composed of Kālī,
just as a spray of water entering the ocean becomes the ocean itself.
In that way, indeed, the splendor of the sun and other luminaries became the splendor of Kālī;
O Goddess, just as various waters, once they have fallen into the Gaṅgā, [become one].
O Goddess of the Gods, everything arises from Gaṅgā alone; likewise, O Maheśvarī, everything is entirely composed of Kālī’s splendor—there is no distinction whatsoever.
Know all that, O Goddess, O beautiful one among the gods, to be immortal;
and her, O Goddess, I bear upon my head day and night, without ceasing.
Therefore, my status as Śaṅkara is indeed certainly and truly established;
for I always bear that Kālī, who extends for five krośas, upon my head.
Day and night, filled with supreme bliss, I worship [you];
therefore, my lordship over the universe is eternal—of this there is no doubt. (36)
O Goddess of the gods, he who is the Lord of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others,
he alone is the Lord of the Universe (Viśveśvara), and no other, O Supreme Goddess.
Having become possessed of absolute bliss, I always worship the Supreme;
there, her grace arose as an incorporeal voice consisting of the Vāgbhava syllable.
The Goddess said: [Kālī said:
"O Lord, supreme bliss has been bestowed upon me by you.
Therefore, grant eternal bliss to those who die in Kāśī. (39)
The Lord said:
Having heard these words of hers, I, submerged in the ocean of nectar,
bestowed the supreme Brahman into the range of the ears of one who was about to die.
O Goddess Śivā, those who, remaining constantly in Vārāṇasī, are devoted to meditation—whether they die in the water, on land, or in the air within Vārāṇasī—[attain liberation]. 41.
I bestow the supreme Brahman upon those who have it within the range of their ears.
For by abandoning all action— both well-done and ill-done—
they shall attain the nirvāṇa of Brahman through my instruction in an instant;
for all that, O Maheśvarī, whether it be well-done or ill-done action, [is thus relinquished].
By the grace of Mahākālī and through the yoga of knowledge, all that becomes reduced to ashes. || 44 ||
For whatever is attached to Kāśī becomes Kāśī at that very moment;
by the mere touch of Kāśī, you shall always be filled with perfect bliss.

O Śivā, just as fire burns a heap of cotton after a short time, so too does Kāśī burn the karma of one who possesses the trident (or suffers from colic) in an instant through the touch of its splendor.
In that same way, a single birth in Kāśī burns away the heap of karma for men;
what more need I tell you regarding the accumulation of merit at the site of Kāśī? 47.
Moreover, O Goddess, if there were a woman equal to you and a man equal to me, then such a person would be capable of describing even a fraction of the fruit of Kāśī. (48)
(117) Those born from eggs, those born from heat, those born from sprouts, and those born from a womb—all of them attain liberation if they die by good fortune in Kāśī. || 49 ||
O Goddess, this auspicious Vārāṇasī is composed of great splendor;
indeed, due to the differences between the Yugas, it is perceived by people in four ways.

In the Kṛta age, Kāśī was composed of jewels; in the Tretā age, it is remembered as being made of gold; in the Dvāpara age, it took the form of stone; and in the Kali age, it is auspiciously composed of earth.
There exists no field superior to this within the three worlds;
truly, truly, O Great Goddess, I tell you this under oath. (52)
O Goddess, he who desires liberation again by way of the path of saṃsāra will remain restrained in Kāśī, due to his greed for Pāṣāṇeśvara.
He alone is wise and possessed of knowledge; he alone is the sanctifier of his lineage.
O Great Goddess, even at the cost of his life, a learned man should never abandon Kāśī.
He alone is the supreme fool; he alone is the destroyer of his lineage—he who, having reached Kāśī, has abandoned it in vain for the sake of the world of fools. 55.
If a person should obtain Kāśī through the merits accumulated over many births,
then they should never abandon Kāśī, even at the end of their life.
He who desires to cross the ocean of saṃsāra without effort should go, even with great exertion, to my city of Vārāṇasī. 57.
One should give food, for Annapūrṇā bestows food; one should give knowledge, for Sarasvatī bestows knowledge;
and by always remaining in Kāśī, I am indeed the giver of liberation at the end of life. 58.
Thus has that which was asked of me been told to you, O Goddess Girijā—this supreme, purifying [teaching on] liberation. What more do you wish to hear from this? (59)
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The seventeenth chapter.
The Goddess said:
O ancient Supreme Lord, you are the teacher of all the worlds; O Sovereign of the transcendent power of the universe, tell me how the Kolas are to be brought down.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the slaying of Kolāsura;
this wonderful account [occurred] in connection with Mahākālī. || 2 ||
Evil arose from the curse of Brahmā upon Viṣṇu of incomparable splendor;
afflicted by that evil, he, the all-knowing one, performed penance.
Having gone to the vicinity of the Himalayas, intent upon the destruction of that sin,
he constantly recited the eight-syllabled great mantra of Mahākālī.
At the end of ten thousand years, that Great Goddess was pleased;
by her mere satisfaction, [Viṣṇu emerged] from the lotus of Viṣṇu’s heart.
Having become an asura among the Kolas, he suddenly emerged;
by that powerful and evil-minded Daitya, everything was carried away.
Having utterly defeated all the gods, beginning with Indra, the great asura seized the abode of Viṣṇu and the lotus-seated Brahmā.
Then Viṣṇu and the other gods, having approached the eternal Kālī, praised her with devotion, being distressed and crying out, "Protect us! Protect us! (7ka)
Kālī said:
"Now listen, O child Viṣṇu! Taking up the form of a maiden and residing in the city of Kolā, I shall slay the Kolas along with their kinsmen. (8)
(119) Īśvara said: Having thus heard Kālī’s words, the gods, headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu,
were submerged in an ocean of bliss and danced intensely like peacocks.
Therefore, O Goddess, Kālī— whose face was formidable and whose hair was like that of a twice-born bird in its natural form—
went to Kolāpura to the presence of the demon Kolāsura; there, as a maiden, she begged that preeminent Daitya for him to be her food.
Kālī said:
"O Great King, I am deprived of my mother and father and abandoned by all companions; I am hungry, so let food be given to me. (11)
Īśvara said: Then, O Goddess, the demon Kolāsura, completely deluded by her illusory power (māyā),
took her by the hand out of compassion and entered the inner apartments himself.
She said, "I shall give you food, whatever you yourself desire;
sit here, O girl, upon this seat adorned with jewels. (13)
Having spoken thus, he gave her various kinds of food many times;
O Goddess, after she had eaten it all, she said, "Give me more. (14)
He gave her even more, and she ate it herself;
as she said, "I am not yet satiated," the Asura Kolahala then spoke to her. (15)

"Perform your meal only so much as will bring satisfaction to the child; such is that [truth],"—having heard these words spoken, Kālī, who had assumed the form of a young girl, [acted accordingly]. (16)
In an instant, Kālī devoured the treasury, the horses, the elephants, the chariot, the army along with its kinsmen, and the exceedingly powerful Kolāsura.
(120) Just as Kālarudra, in due time, would pass through the three ages beginning with a *kṣaṇa*, so too, O Śivā, Kolāpura was rendered empty by Kālī in an instant. 18.
Then the gods, headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, having had their enemies slain,
showered a continuous rain of flowers and danced most excellently.
The gods, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras sang a most charming song;
and the Apsarases, the wives of the gods, were surrounded on all sides by Kinnarīs.
That maiden was worshipped by them with flowers born in the Nandana grove;
and that maiden was worshipped in every house by those who were not present in all the worlds.
Then that goddess, the maiden whose form is Brahman, vanished.
Thus have I today told you of the slaying of the demon Kola.
The curse of a Brahmin is difficult to overcome; therefore, one should never act against that venerable brahmin.
O passionate woman, always recognize that the speech of Brahmins is like a thunderbolt. (23)
Therefore, O Goddess, whether ignorant or possessed of knowledge, one should always remain a Brāhmaṇa;
by being satisfied with the Brāhmaṇas, we gods are always satisfied.
O Goddess, when a Brāhmaṇa is displeased, we ourselves are indeed displeased;
for even if a Brāhmaṇa were to personally commit a hundred improper acts, O Goddess, [the fault remains with us]. (25)
Nevertheless, one who desires his own welfare should not abandon him;
nor should he ever show him contempt, O foremost of gods. (26)
The Brāhmaṇa is indeed the soul of all gods and is equal to the splendor of liberation;
and that Kālī, who assumes the form of a maiden, is childless.
From that time forward, O Goddess of gods, the Kumārī is worshipped by the deities;
the Kumārī is always worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the others.
(121) O beautiful one, she would be honored by all others within the entire realm of the cosmic egg;
I am not able to describe the fruit of worshipping a maiden. 29.
Even with thousands of tongues and hundreds of millions of words,
one should therefore worship Bālā, who arises from all castes.
O Śivā, no distinction of caste should be made in the worship of the maiden;
O Maheśānī, due to such a distinction of caste, one does not return from hell. (31)
A practitioner who is overcome by doubt will certainly become a sinner;
therefore, one should worship her with the perception that she is the Goddess and with great devotion. || 32 ||
For the maiden is indeed the embodiment of all vidyās; there is no doubt in this matter.
When the one young girl is worshipped, O God, the worship of all has been performed. (33)
By worshipping her alone, there would be the worship of the three worlds.
O Goddess, O Beloved, if by the power of fortune a practitioner obtains a maiden born of a courtesan's family, he should seek her even at the cost of his entire possessions. (34)
One should worship her with effort and joy using gold, silver, and other materials;
then great accomplishment arises for him, of this there is no doubt. || 35 ||
Great accomplishment shall be his; having become one with Sadāśiva, he dissolves into my body—he indeed is the venerable Sadāśiva.
I shall describe his characteristics; listen to that, as well as those of the practitioner who is a maiden.
Priyamvadā! || 36 ||
O Great Goddess, the body of one who has been thus cut becomes like gold;
having attained all siddhis, he sports like Bhairava himself. 37.
His movement in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld is certain;
indeed, everything that exists in his mind comes to pass through sheer force.
Having attained this body, which is a manifestation of the [divine] form, one becomes all-pervading;
with unimpeded command everywhere, just like Purandara, O Śivā. (39)
The wives of the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, nāgas, and kinnaras, as well as vidyādharīs and royal women, attend upon him day and night. (40)
And before that, he attains the supreme, ultimate Nirvāṇa;
at the time of worshipping the Kumārī, the practitioner shall attain the state of Śiva.
Wherever the Kumārī is worshipped, that region becomes a purifier of the earth;
it shall become most meritorious for five krośas in every direction. || 42 ||
O Supreme Goddess, wherever the Kumārī is worshipped, one should perform worship there;
for in that place, the great light— her radiant splendor— manifests visibly upon the land of Bhārata.
A king named Viśvaṃbhara, born of the Caitra dynasty,
honored that maiden who was born of a family of courtesans.
O Great Goddess, at the time of worship, one should obtain Kāñcī— she who is named Kāñcī, dark-complexioned, and endowed with all auspicious marks— who possesses a shimmering radiance.
Enveloped by the mass of her splendor, the king [becomes so].
He attained liberation.
There, the light consisting of pure radiance, the eternal Kāñcī, having become fully perfected, always accepts worship in that place—indeed, in his very dream. (46)
The city named Kāñcī was born; that location is of great fruit.
That auspicious city, extending for five krośas, should be known as the bestower of liberation. (47)
O Daughter of the Mountain King, whatever household duties and such may have been performed there, all that constitutes worship for her; this is truly marvelous. (48)
Then, O Goddess, the auspicious city of Kāñcī was purified, as was the beautiful Vārāṇasī;
thus was Bālā worshipped by the high-souled Kampilla.
O fair-faced one, having previously arisen there in the city of Kāmpilya,
she is seen even today in the world, remaining in the form of a stone.
O Goddess, it is the most meritorious of all dwellings, crowded with all sacred fords, endowed with all sacrifices, and surrounded by great sages.

Those who dwell in the city of Kāmpilya, which is filled with all sovereignty and pervaded by every wonder— those who reside in the supreme city of Kāmpilya, O Great Goddess, at the forefront of Kāmpilla. (52)
Having enjoyed here these excellent yogas that grant me satisfaction,
and being endowed with all prosperity in the end through the grace of the Goddess— (53)
Having indeed transcended the world of Brahmā, they shall attain the abode of the Goddess;
if anyone should have the desire, he may go to the supreme Vaikuṇṭha.

O Maheśānī, just as my palace of jewels is like the world of the gods, so too have I today related this account of Kumārī’s life to you, O Śivā; such is it, O Mahāmāyā—what more could possibly be told? (55)
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the glorious Yoginītantra, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The eighteenth chapter.
The Goddess said:
"The conduct of Kumārī, which was previously desired by the gods, has indeed been heard. Now I wish to hear the supreme account of Kahola."
Command that, O Mahādeva, out of supreme compassion; for it is indeed for the benefit of all the worlds and grants the heart's desire of the yogins. (2)
Īśvara said:
He is the possessor of the Vedas, Vedāntas, and Vedāṅgas, the embodiment of all scriptures;
he is the performer of all sacrifices, the Lord of all yogīs, the Divine One, free from all sins.
Having attained mastery over all sciences and mantras, the achiever of all goals, Kahola, the best of sages, wandered the earth; purified by all sacred fords, he was devoid of all worldly objects.
A perfected master of all sciences and all mantras, a lord among seers,
the most excellent and best of sages, he wandered across the earth.
O Śivā, he who formerly possessed the splendor of a thousand suns fell into great anxiety, his mind exceedingly agitated.
O best among the wise, he became intensely tormented by supreme anxiety, his body wasting away without interruption;
then, a voice arising from the sky was heard by the great seer.

O Kahola, protect [the eastern direction]; as the god Maheśvara is the benefactor (Śaṅkara) of the gods in the east, so may that Guru perform everything for you—he who is the teacher of all sentient beings. || 7 ||
Having heard that celestial voice, Kahola was overwhelmed with supreme bliss;
he went and related that entire account to me. (8)
Then I bestowed upon him the supreme Kālī-vidyā, the highest digit (kalā),
consisting of the syllables of the moon, the source of all knowledge, composed of consciousness, and auspicious.
And the supreme conduct arising from the glorious Āgama was bestowed upon him;
and it was explained by me to that son of Kahola—listen to that. (10)
Having gone to Kāśī by means of this practice of conduct, he who meditates upon and worships the naked Kālī, the destroyer of all ignorance— || 11 ||
Then, O Bhuvaneśvarī, their doubts would be destroyed;
thus was that sage Kahola, an expert in the Vedas, commanded by the Lord of the World. 12.
Having gone to Kāśī, one should joyfully worship Kālī while adhering to the fivefold conduct;
his doubts and obstacles will flee day by day.

"O sage, [granting all desired objects to everyone]," thus commanded, that sage Kahola, an expert in the Vedas, went to Kāśī and joyfully worshipped Kālī while observing the fivefold conduct. [This additional portion is found in manuscript Kha. Of Kahola, the embodiment of the Veda and the high-minded one...
Then, auspicious compassion arose in Mahākālī toward that sage.
And so, O Goddess, through compassion, the most excellent sage Kahola attained the Self, which is the form of Kālikā, the supreme, eternal Brahman. (15)
In Śiva, there arose supreme non-dual knowledge, free from all illusion;
that most excellent sage was born entirely liberated from all māyā. (16)
Having seen this entire world, including all that is moving and unmoving, as consisting of Brahman, one never perceives anything such as one's own body or self at any time. (17)
By that very knowledge of Brahman, O Maheśānī, the body, karma,
and so forth of that great-souled sage were indeed reduced to ashes.
The sage Kahola, having become one with Brahman through the grace of Mahākālī, may he be devoted to all transgressive practices, for he indeed vibrates [with divine power]. 19.
In this very way, Mahākālī struck the sage Kahola, the son of Kahola;
she then caused that sage to become absorbed within her own causal body.
Whatever state a practitioner relies upon when worshipping Kālī,
O Goddess, he shall obtain that very fruit without delay through the grace of Mahākālī.
The Goddess said:
"I have heard the former, wondrous account of Kahola’s conduct, as well as that of the gods, asuras, lords of sages, and seers of purified souls. (22)
Now I wish to hear about Gaṅgā, the purifier of the three worlds;
having acquired what knowledge did she become so? Tell me that, O Lord. (23)
The Lord said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain that which you ask of me;
by hearing it, all sins go to destruction, and not otherwise. (24)
First, I shall proclaim the mantra named "Purifier of the Three Worlds," which was spoken by Mahādeva to the Great Goddess Mahākālī. (25)
Having extracted one's own seed-syllable and two words of address, and again one's own seed-syllable—this supreme Vidyā brings about fame. (26)
Having propitiated this Vidyā, Gaṅgā, the purifier of the three worlds, remained upon the slope of my matted locks and recited the Vidyā day and night. || 27 ||
Therefore, that purifying Gaṅgā, who grants liberation to all embodied beings, was greatly augmented in her splendor by Kālī through the power of her perfected mantra-nature. (28)
Therefore, having become purifying, she shall always grant liberation to Śiva (and to Sadāśiva);
for this reason, that Vidyā is worshipped by all among all sacred fords (tīrthas). || 29 ||
O Goddess of the gods, how can I possibly describe the majesty of the Gaṅgā, by the mere remembrance of whose name even sinners become partakers of liberation? (30)
Even if one who is himself a sinner among sinners should utter "Gaṅgā, Gaṅgā," he shall cast off their sins and go indeed to the city of Viṣṇu.
O Maheśvarī, whatever sins have been described by you—
whether they are devoid of expiation or even those for which expiation has been prescribed— one who desires dharma, wealth, and liberation must not abandon that place. (32)
All of those perish through the sprinkling of the waters of the Gaṅgā.
O Goddess, that auspicious Gaṅgā which always flows toward the city—if one should cause the Gaṅgā to flow from a different location—[it would bring great merit]. || 33 ||
O Śivā, by the greatness of the mantra, everything indeed becomes the Gaṅgā;
that land where the Gaṅgā flows becomes a vessel of merit.
(128) This sacred field, extending for two *yojanas*, is declared to be pure; it is designated as the site where even minor sins, secondary sins, and great sins are purified.
Whatever rite is performed there is equivalent to one performed on the Gaṅgā; of this there is no doubt. (35)

O Goddess, whatever is performed at the Gaṅgā, O beloved of Śambhu, that shall yield inexhaustible fruit—whether it be complete with all its constituent parts or devoid of them; so it has been declared. (36)
All the living beings residing there have emerged from the world of the gods;
having always performed meritorious deeds, they enjoy various pleasures.
Without effort they shall go to that place which is most difficult to attain, where the flow of the Gaṅgā exists, praised by the hosts of gods and sages. (38)
He who gives up his life in the Gaṅgā by virtue of his meritorious nature attains liberation through knowledge; by the power of that [act], he reaches Vaikuṇṭha. (39)
O Maheśānī, the worlds beginning with Svarga are conquered of their sins by the Gaṅgā;
whoever, having set out for the Gaṅgā, gives up his life on the way, [attains those worlds]. || 40 ||
Even a sinner goes to the world of Viṣṇu, which abounds in virtues, if he gives up his life on its bank—whether by lawful means or even by unlawful means. (41)
He too attains heaven, endowed with all provisions,
as long as the bones of the deceased remain cast into the Gaṅgā.
For as many thousands of years as there are particles of Gaṅgā water mixed with his body, he is honored in the heavenly world, wherever he may die.
Freed from all sins, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
With a concentrated mind, one should offer a funeral cake (piṇḍa) on the bank of the Gaṅgā at a spot four cubits wide. (44)
Having performed the rite of expiation for his ancestors, that man shall dwell in the world of Viṣṇu. || 45 ||
O Goddess, for that meritorious person who performs the libation (tarpaṇa) in the Gaṅgā, there will truly be great satisfaction for the ancestors for a hundred years. (46)
It has been declared in the same way for the sages and the deities:
whether by day or by night, at the junction of day and night (saṃdhyā) or in the dead of night. || 47 ||
O Śivā, one should perform bathing, giving, austerity, fire-offerings, libations, and worship at the Gaṅgā; one should not observe distinctions regarding the time.
O Śivā, if one should abandon their ritual duty after having observed the lapse of time,
they shall become an immobile being in the forest; indeed, having become such, he is born in the woods, and thereafter,
his body is consumed in many ways by the crest of a forest fire.
But death is of many kinds;
at its conclusion, O Supreme Goddess, one becomes a Cāṇḍāla, eternally miserable.
He is born for seven lifetimes, and at their end, he becomes a washerman; O Maheśānī, for three more births, and at their end, he is born among the Śūdra wombs.
O Great Goddess, after ten births one indeed attains the status of a Vaiśya;
after four births have passed, one attains the status of a Kṣatriya, and after three births, [the status of a Brāhmaṇa].
Having thereby attained the status of a Brāhmaṇa, that man shall obtain a meritorious rebirth;
for he who takes away anything from the Gaṅgā, O Supreme Goddess, [incurs great sin].
O Goddess, O Sovereign of the Gods, there is no atonement for that blinding darkness of delusion, which leads to the Raurava hell, until the dissolution of all beings; thus has it been told to you.
O passionate woman, that man who accepts [gifts] on her bank— or indeed on the bank of the Gaṅgā, or from the Gaṅgā itself— is born constantly as a dog-eater (outcaste) for ten lifetimes. (55)
Then, due to the fault of poverty, he wanders the earth for seven births, O Great Goddess; at the end of that time, he shall obtain liberation.
Thus, O Great Goddess, has the supreme majesty of the mantra of that Kālikā been told to you, as well as the reason for the majesty of Gaṅgā.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
The nineteenth chapter.
The Goddess said: O Lord, ocean of compassion and supreme bliss,
for those fallen into this shoreless and terrible great ocean of saṃsāra, || 1 ||
Who else but you exists within the sphere of the universe to be the deliverer of those who have died?
For you are considered by all beings, beginning with Brahmā, to be the Guru. (2)
I ask you, O Lord; please speak out of supreme compassion.
O Lord of the World, everything has been heard by me from the lotus of your mouth. (3)
Now I wish to hear that which has occupied my mind: relying upon what knowledge did Karālabhairava himself [act]? (4)
(131) Krodhavaktra became Bhairava, the bestower of fear upon all beings;
indeed, from him gods, asuras, and others fled, afflicted by terror. || 5 ||
They protect their respective splendors and their own beings here and there;
O Lord, O Digambara, I wish to hear about that knowledge—please speak.
Īśvara said:
This great vidyā is exceedingly secret; indeed, it is more secret than the secret.
It is the very essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others, to be cherished for as long as life lasts.
O Supreme Goddess, one is simply unable to describe that Vidyā;
O Kulabhairavī, let it be known that only its name is being uttered.
Where indeed, O Supreme Goddess, resides Sundarī, the bestower of boons, the Queen of Vidyās, Ghorakālī, and Aniruddhasarasvatī. || 9 ||

Having received that Great Vidyā, which had issued from the mouth of his Guru, that Bhairava, the Primordial Lord, together with Mahākālabhairava and the others, [received it]. (The reading *śrīmukhāniḥsṛtā* is also attested.)
O Great Goddess, merely by attaining him, Karālabhairava always considered himself purified and superior to all others. (11)
Liberated from all of saṃsāra and worshipped by the gods beginning with Brahmā,
he performed extremely difficult austerities on the eastern Udayācala mountain.
O Goddess, having become one whose feet were half-grown, for two hundred thousand years.
One hundred thousand [verses] are on Himācala, one hundred thousand on Mandarācala, likewise one hundred thousand at Kanakāśrama, and two hundred thousand at Uḍḍīyāna. (13)
And likewise, O Śivā, there are twenty-five lakhs in Jālandhara;
and on Puṇyaśaila, there are likewise one lakh measured at twenty-five [thousand].
And for twenty-five hundred thousand years, he performed this most difficult penance for ten million years within the yoni-maṇḍala of Kāmākhyā. (15)
O Goddess, although you performed that [rite] with great hardship and with the most terrifying Karāla-Bhairava,
Kālī was never at all pleased with him.
Then, O Goddess Śivā, that Bhairava went into the presence of his guru and reported the account of his ascetic penance.
O Supreme Goddess, having heard this, the illustrious Ādinātha, Mahākāla, Maheśvara,
and my own Lord have come under the power of meditative realization.
Without the supreme conduct, I declare that there will indeed be no accomplishment; this is the summary.
But how can I explain the supreme conduct to you in detail? (19)
This alone is the supreme practice, united with the heart of Kālī;
it is the secret of secrets, beyond the reach of Brahmā and the other gods.
This is the direct bestower of liberation, the granter of all perfections and boons;
it is the manifest seed-mantra of Kālī and my very everything.
All this has been told by Śiva: "One who is tranquil in being and a great yogi shall become equal to me; therefore, he must be protected by him with great effort. (22)
For the sake of proper conduct, my own foot was offered to Kālarudra;
for this is indeed my everything—Śambhu, though free from agitation, took his own place from me, who am mindless.
One should practice such conduct by means of extreme secrecy; for the wise one, the knowledge of reality is hidden within right conduct. (24)
The Lord of all, the kinsman of the universe, Sadāśiva, has attained freedom from old age and death; he is the Great Peace, the Supreme Sovereign. (25)
Then, seeing him constantly devoted to that conduct and tranquil,
I once again bestowed upon him my own station and the office of Guru in brief.
I indeed always abide joyfully within his body;
however, I abide in the supreme thousand-petaled lotus of all beings.
Having attained the entire state of Śiva, I indeed abide forever as Śiva;
may Śiva be auspicious, for there is never any difference from Śiva anywhere at all. || 28 ||
Since he is the preceptor even of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others, he is therefore Śiva; he too is peaceful, a great yogi, and truly capable of right conduct.
No one else anywhere is ever capable of that conduct;
only through the grace of Śiva is the practitioner capable of it. (30)
Forgiveness is the goddess Girijā, the daughter of the mountain; she is never anyone else.
And this one above is always Karālabhairava, whose deeds are formidable.
How may one know that very supreme conduct so as to be capable of protecting it from darkness?
For this conduct alone is indeed like my own worship of Kālikā.
Having propitiated the Queen of Wisdom (Vidyārājñī), I may perhaps become worthy to bestow her;
yet I am not worthy to bestow the supreme conduct that reaches the very heart of Kālī.
Having thus honored and reflected upon this, my lord commanded Karālabhairava:
"Go, my son, toward Trilocana. (34)
(134) Nevertheless, the Goddess, who is composed of compassion, ascended Śiva;
then that Bhairava himself went into the presence of his mother Kālikā. 35.
Having abandoned all austerity, contemplating thus within his inner self:
"Whatever has been muttered and whatever austerity performed—let it indeed go, let it go; for that is truly in vain. (36)
"By the power of my fate, that command of my preceptor would indeed become fruitless;
therefore, I shall abandon this body, for I will never speak [against it] again. (37)
Having made such a vow, he was intent on abandoning his body;
then this voice arose from the sky and was uttered: || 38 ||
It was heard by that noble-souled Karāla Bhairava;
O Mistress, I shall declare that command to you—having heard it, listen to my command regarding your own portion. || 39 ||
O best of Bhairavas, may your command to me indeed become fruitless.
"Since you have always practiced penance without proper conduct for the sake of self-knowledge, how can I grant you great siddhi or even a vision of myself? (41)
Go once more to Mahākālabhairava, the destroyer of worldly existence; he is your primordial lord and guru, and he will relate such a narrative to you.
Then he will certainly bestow upon you the Great Conduct (mahācāra). || 43 ||
"O God of excellent vows, because of that very conduct of yours, you are indeed intent upon my propitiation;
therefore, I shall soon grant whatever dwells in your mind. (44)
The auspicious great mantra of Kālītārā and the certain mantra of Vidyā—whosoever recites these without the Kulācāra practice shall indeed become a denizen of hell. || 45 ||
"How can there be accomplishment for him? Liberation remains far away.
Thus did the Command speak through a voice from the sky to Bhairava. Having heard this from Mahākālī, that supreme Bhairava attained it. (46) [This additional passage is found in manuscript KHA.]
And having gone again to the illustrious Lord, the Primordial Lord, the Great Master, Mahākāla, the Great God, whose form is emptiness, the Teacher of the World; || 47 ||
He then reported whatever words had been spoken; at that moment, Mahākālī’s compassion arose toward Karālabhairava. [The mother Mahākālī’s compassion was directed toward Karālabhairava. || 48 ||
Thinking thus, he was censured by the Guru who is of the nature of the Void; then Karālabhairava, the Teacher of the World who is likewise of the nature of the Void, spoke with due restraint. (49)
Mahākāla, the Lord of the World, indeed consecrated that supreme, secret family tradition which was proclaimed in the Kālītantra. (50)
Through the rite of Śākta initiation and likewise through the full consecration (pūrṇābhiṣeka),
the highly renowned Krodhavaktra bestowed a name upon Karāla.
Having caused [the disciple] to hear of the divine state, immediately thereafter the heroic state;
[he should offer] wine, fish, and the seal, along with a vessel filled with the causal [substances]. (52)
The Guru Mahākāla himself, appearing in an empty form, bestowed [the deity] Mahākāla upon him;
at that time, this entire world of moving and unmoving beings shone forth.
Then, O Goddess, even Krodhavaktra, having bowed at the lotus feet of Śrī Mahākālī and having recollected the Śrī Gurupādukā of Mahākālī, [remained there]. (54)
(136) Having accepted the supreme cause with devotion through the command of the Guru,
his sins destroyed, possessing all-encompassing wisdom, radiant, steady-minded,
and filled with supreme bliss. (55)
O Goddess, King Krodha is submerged in an ocean of bliss;
O Maheśānī, having bowed again at the feet of the Guru, he [is absorbed] in the Śakti-kopa (or Śaktipāda). 56.
Remaining in the ocean of worldly existence, he praised [him] with supreme devotion. || 57 ||
Krodhavaktrabhairava said:
I bow to the Lord, the wish-fulfilling tree for the gods, the Guru who is the great incarnation of consciousness and bliss;
he is eternally the nature of pure knowledge and bliss, the Supreme Brahman beyond the supreme, whose very form is Śiva. (58)
The abode of the world, the primordial root of the universe, the one unknown known as the Supreme Self—
[the remainder]: consisting of light, the nature of the partless reality, devoid of action, the supreme and stainless.
[Serene] || 59 ||

Free from conceptual proliferation, of perfect nature, empty of beginning and end, beyond primordial matter (prakṛti), possessing form though formless, clearly manifest as the truth—the compassionate descent, indeed the very embodiment of emptiness. || 60 ||

I perpetually bow to the Guru, the seed for the destruction of beginningless saṃsāra, the supreme purifier, who is indeed beyond the reach of the senses; he whose heart is Śiva, whose nature is pure light, and who is the mantra of the absolute Name. (61)
The wise one beholds you, who are subtler than the subtle and greater than the great, like the sun in the sky;
for that eye born of knowledge is itself the truth, and he, O Lord, has truly entered into you.
I bow today to that ancient Primeval Person, who enables one to cross the essence-less ocean of saṃsāra;
I likewise pay homage to Kālī, the seed of the supreme truth, and to her lotus-like feet.
O Sādhaka, whoever shall praise you with devotion by means of this hymn—at dawn, at midday, and at evening—become the bestower of liberation for them. (64)
Mahākālabhairava said:
"O my son, I am always pleased with this hymn of yours;
go quickly to the Yonipīṭha, taking refuge on the peak of the Goddess."
Devote yourself to Kālī, being intent on the state of passion for the Kula practice;
before long, the desired perfection will be yours—of this there is no doubt.
"When shall I see the heroic practitioner situated in the midst of courtesans?
Thus spoke that Kālī; therefore, become devoted to courtesans.
For in the practice of mantra, there is never any fault anywhere;
therefore, abandoning delusion, take refuge in the Kula dharma. 68.
One must not entertain doubt in this regard, for it would lead to the loss of accomplishment.
If one possesses a pure mind, accomplishment will be attained even within half an eon.
Īśvara said:
Then, having gone there and joyfully bowed many times to Mahākālī and his guru,
he reached the Yonipīṭha and took refuge on the peak of Devī.
Having become devoted to the five types of courtesans—Urvaśī, Menakā, Rambhā, Pañcacūḍā, and Tilottamā—he remained dedicated to the conduct of his lineage. (71)
The Lord of Wrath (Krodhabhūpati) recited the Mahāvidyā, pure in essence—the Queen of Vidyās, Ghorakālī Aniruddha-Sarasvatī. || 72 ||
By means of exactly one hundred and eight [recitations], she becomes manifest to him—Kālī, whose face is formidable, whose form is splendor, and who is eternal. (73)
(138) Constantly overspreading the entire circle of the cosmic egg with his splendor, Bhairava, beholding that immense radiance, was overwhelmed with fear. || 74 ||
Lacking the proper means and having fainted, he fell from the mountain to the earth.
Then Kālī, the Mother of the World and a vast ocean of compassion,
consoled that Krodha and spoke to him with words like nectar.
Then,
having risen, Bhairava, his body covered in horripilation,
praised the Goddess with supreme devotion through various kinds of rites.
Bowing down again and again, he then spoke to Kālī.
Krodhavaktra said:
"O Supreme Brahman, O Supreme Abode, O Eternal Supreme Self, you who consist of mind, grant me forever that which my heart desires. (77)
Kālī said:
"O most excellent Bhairava, may you indeed be the eternal restrainer of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others, as well as those who dwell outside the cosmic egg. (78)
O son, whoever worships me according to the family tradition shall attain the status of my own son; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. (79)
"Accept my mouth; you are the one who causes fear even to the cosmic egg (Brahmāṇḍa).
Your mouth is the supreme form of Time (Kāla), the restrainer of all. (80)
Īśvara said:
Having given her face to Bhairava, Śivā attained peace in an instant;
Mahākāla and Bhairava also became Vajrapāṇi.
Through the grace of Mahākālī, he—known by the name Īśvara and possessing the vajra in his hand—became Karālabhairava in form with a wrathful face. (82)
Thus, O auspicious lady, has been told by me in the first half of the Śrīyoginītantra;
it should always be kept secret, just as one's own vulva is protected from another man. (83)
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the *Yoginītantra*, the great king of tantras, in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
Thus ends the first section of the glorious *Yoginītantra*.
Uttara-khaṇḍa, First Paṭala:
Oṃ, salutation to Kāmākhyā. [Salutation to Kāmākhyā.]

May that supreme Light, which is Māyā, protect the worlds eternally— she who, though manifest here through Vidyā, exists as a conceptual construction based on the primary substrate (pradhāna), because the three worlds have existence as their inherent nature.
The Goddess said:
"O beloved of my life, I have heard of the sacred seats (pīṭhas) beginning with Uḍḍīyāna;
now I desire to hear the definitive description of Kāmarūpa. (2)
O Lord, as you have said to me, that sacred seat (pīṭha) known as Kāmākhyā— which destroys terrible sins— is clearly manifest and is considered to have come forth in the Kali age. (3)
O Lord, O All-pervading One, tell me what is that supreme medicine which acts as the healer for the various fangs of the black serpent of the Kali age? 4.
The Blessed One said:
"O Goddess of the Gods, the manifestation of Uḍḍīyāna occurred in the Kṛta Yuga;
the origin of Pūrṇaśaila took place at the beginning of the Tretā Yuga. (5)
O Maheśvarī, in the Dvāpara age it was that of Jālaśaila, and in the Kali age it is that of Kāmākhyā, for the destruction of the terrible sins of the Kali age.

Every year, for each successive age, there is your sacred seat (*pīṭha*) and its secondary seat (*upapīṭha*); likewise, for each triad of ages, there is a great field (*mahākṣetra*) and a holy forest (*puṇyāraṇya*). (7)
In every shrine is Mahādeva; in every shrine is the four-armed one;
in every shrine resides Gaṅgā, and in every shrine is Pārvatī.
In the Kali age, at every sacred seat (pīṭha), in every field, and even in a holy forest within a village,
people develop the notion that it is a pilgrimage site (tīrtha) only when it is very far from their home.
However, the sacred fords (tīrthas) indeed exist within the temple of the perfection of devotion;
at every seat (pīṭha), the doctrine is distinct and the conduct is likewise distinct.
In every land, the local family traditions must not be destroyed by arguments;
there are distinct modes of worship, distinct mantras, and the Tārapīṭha among mortals.
Bhadrapīṭha is in the south, O Pārvatī;
Jālandhara is in the west, and Pūrṇapīṭha is in the east. (12)
Know that Kāmarūpa is in the northeast and the eastern part; Jālandhara is in the northwest, and Kolāpura is in the north. (13)
In the northeast is the Vihāra, and Mahendra is somewhat to the north; Śrīhaṭṭa is also in the east. Now hear of the secondary seats (upapīṭhas).
O Goddess of gods, by means of a boat-vehicle, it would take sixty-eight yojanas; in the extent of the Oḍra-pīṭha’s expanse, it would be exceedingly vast. || 15 ||
The pedestal is shaped like a cart, four-cornered, provided with a base, endowed with four doors, and marked with the emblem of the wind-mandala. || 16 ||
The seat of Sindhubhadra is joined by twenty million sacred fords (tīrthas);
there is the Someśvara Liṅga, as well as the supreme Ādipīṭha.
p. 142) Wherever Kāmadhenu and Hara, the Lord of the Wheel, reside, that is the sacred field known as Viraja; immediately following that is Ekāmra. || 18 ||
The great sacred field of Bhāskara, where Mātaṅgaśaṅkara [Bhāskara] resides;
the highly meritorious Kuśasthalī, and likewise the Daṇḍaka forest. || 19 ||
Likewise, Sumanta and Śivayūpa are to the east;
Dhenukāraṇya is to the west, and Gayāśiras is to the north.
To the south is the Candrabhāgā and the Oḍra-pīṭha, O fair-faced one;
it is thirty yojanas in width and a hundred yojanas in length.
Where the goddess Kāmeśvarī resides, whose very nature is the Yonimudrā; where indeed is the sacred seat named Bhūgolapīṭhaka, and where is Golakeśvara.
The Dharma-seat, the Great Seat, where Hara is Kāmeśvara;
likewise Avimukta, the Great Field, and Haṃsaprapatana. || 23 ||
The Brahma-yūpa is in that very place where the Śveta-vaṭa tree stands;
Kurukṣetra is in that very place where the river Māyā-svanā flows.
The meritorious Ayodhyāraṇyaka, as well as the supreme Dharmāraṇya, and the great forest of Kacātmaka; there resides Pātālaśaṅkara.
The Gaṇḍakī river is to the east, and Viṣṇuyūpa is to the west;
the Vṛṣabha Liṅga is to the south, and the Kadalīvana grove is to the north.
One should meditate upon this most excellent seat, shaped like a bow and delightful, as being like the face of a lotus and red in color. (27)
The excellent triangular seat (pīṭha) measures eleven hundred and nine yojanas in length, and eighty-eight [yojanas] in its extent. (28)
There is the excellent Pīṭhaka, as well as the Aśoka seat;
also the great field of Sītā and the hermitage of Agastya.
O beloved, these three fields are the supreme field of Hara:
the field of Mādhava-araṇyaka and likewise the field of Hara-araṇyaka.
The forest of Bharga is indeed this Tri-āraṇyaka;
to the north is the Brahmakṣetra, and to the south it extends as far as the ocean.
To the east is Udayakūṭa and to the west, O beloved, is Śrīparvata;
situated between these two is the sacred seat (pīṭha) known by the name Puṇyākhya.
Traveling from one footprint to another, or at most a distance of two intermediate handspans, and traveling on the night of Śivarātri— this constitutes a month by the solar calendar.
One should know Kāmarūpa as having a six-cornered mango-womb;
you should know that its merit is equal to that of the ninefold array with its three mandalas.
The center of the altar is proclaimed to be joined with ten mountains;
it is the central seat, the great seat, where Kāmeśvara resides. (35)
O Goddess of gods, in that sacred seat (pīṭha) where the river Campāvatī flows,
there is the great field of Kanyāśrama, where the two feet of Rudra are located.
Ekāmra is the supreme sacred field where Śaṅkara is marked by the serpent [Śaṅkara known as Nāga];
and Mānasa is the sacred field where Hara is Viśveśvara.
The Nāṭakāraṇyaka and likewise the Campakāraṇyaka, as well as the Picchilā which is to the south of Gautama and yields great fruit. || 38 ||
To the east, as far as the river Svarṇanadī; to the west, the Karatoyā; to the south, Mount Mandaśaila; and to the north, Mount Vihagācala. (39)
In the Prastāra [arrangement], it is half a month, five yojanas,
thirty thousand [yojanas], and likewise ten times that which arises from the five-fold three-streams.

And where there is an eight-cornered emerald [casket] in which the Goddess who dwells in the quarters resides—whether through knowledge, meditation, or even through worldly existence—in that very place she abides. (41)
They too attain stability through the grace of the Goddess, and not otherwise.
Now, the first [or rising] new seat is called the Saumāra human seat (mānavapīṭha). || 42 ||
There, the invisible Dikkaravāsinī dwells in direct perception; and to the northwest of that Dikkarasthāna is the exceedingly rare Nīlapīṭha.
Where the goddess Kāmeśvarī exists in the form of the Yonimudrā,
there is the great sacred field (kṣetra) of Pārijāta, where Āditya is indeed Śaṅkara.
Kauśeya, Pura, Kṣetra, as well as Cāmarakaṇṭaka,
Āraṇya, Āśvina, and the auspicious Gautamāraṇyaka. || 45 ||
O beloved, hear the extent of the sacred seat (pīṭha) of Śivinātha in the forest:
to the east is the Sauraśilā forest, and to the west is the auspicious Svarṇadī river.
To the south is the Brahma-yūpa, and to the north is Lake Mānasa;
situated between these is the sacred seat (pīṭha), which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 47 ||
The great pīṭha named Saumā is hexagonal and possesses three auspicious circles (or mandalas);
it extends for a thousand yojanas and is the fifth, consisting of horses and copper. 48.
In the *prastāra*, however, that which is devoid of the *vyāsa* is proclaimed as the *kolāpīṭha*;
the great *pīṭha* named *saumā* and the *śivatattva-pīṭha*. (49)
Where indeed is the Vakraśaiveśvara Liṅga and the Kamalā stone;
where is the primary Kedāra-kṣetra and Kedāra-Śaṅkara. || 50 ||
Where there is the Piṇḍakara field where Aruṇa resides,
as well as Durgāraṇya, Somāraṇya, and likewise Bhadrāraṇya.
The great sacred field named Cauhāra extends eighty yojanas by thirty-six yojanas; having gone there, one does not grieve.
The Brahmakṣetra, the Kalākṣetra, and likewise the Raghukṣetra;
the Nandana, the Pārijāta, and furthermore the supreme Śivāraṇya. || 53 ||
O beloved, the region from there up to the seven sacred seats (pīṭhas) is called Deśāraṇya;
to the east, however, the most meritorious river named Hīrikā is remembered.
In the west is the Nāthaka-liṅga, in the north is Mount Kili, and in the south is the Nātha-tree; this is proclaimed as the Pīṭha.
By means of a vehicle, it takes three months and likewise three days;
however, on foot, it takes one month less—that is known by the name Tripīṭha. || 56 ||
Vārāhī is the first sacred seat (pīṭha), and Kolapīṭha is the second;
Kumārakṣetra is the first, and the non-dual Nandana is the second. (57)
The third is the eternal field, Mātaṅga, the first forest;
Siddhāraṇya is the second, and Vipula-vana is the third. || 58 ||
The Liṅga is joined with ten million times ten million [manifestations] and surrounded by hosts of ten million times ten million;
there are five sacred bathing places (tīrthas) to the east, and to the west is the river Dhanadā.
To the south is the place called Patra, and to the north is Kurukāvana;
situated between these two, O Goddess, is that which is known by the name Śrīpīṭha. (60)

Thus ends the first chapter in the second part of the first [section], in the section on the Kāmarūpa Pīṭha, within the twenty-two thousand [verse] *Yoginītantra*, which is the most supreme among all tantras.
Chapter Two.
The Blessed One said:

Having constantly performed the rites for the ancestors, including the Nāndīmukha ancestors, in one's own home, having worshipped them according to the rules with devotion, one should thereafter undertake the journey. (1)
When Venus is situated in the northern part [of the zodiac] and is favorable along with other auspicious planets,
one should seek permission from one's preceptor and father, and especially from the Brahmins.
Having fed seven brahmins, one should then undertake the journey;
however, one should not go to the eastern seat during the months of Leo, Sagittarius, or Aries.
A wise man should not go to the western house when the moon is in the signs of Aquarius, Libra, Gemini, or Aquarius;
nor should he go to the southern house when it is in Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn. || 4 ||
A wise person should not travel north during the months of Cancer, Leo, and Pisces.
One should not go toward the southeast when the moon is in Sagittarius, Virgo, or Libra;
one should avoid the southwest when it is in Capricorn, Cancer, or Pisces.
One should avoid [the practice] in the northwest when the zodiac sign is Aquarius, Aries, or Sagittarius;
nor should one contemplate it in the northeast when the sign is Leo, Pisces, or Cancer. (7)
One should understand this as the gross [level]; now hear about the Yoginī, O Śaṅkarī!
O my beloved, one should not go to the eastern region on a Saturday.
One should face the western direction on Sunday, the southern on Wednesday, and likewise the northern on Tuesday; one should also resort to the northern direction on Wednesday.
On a Wednesday, however, it is in the southwest; on Friday, in the northwest;
on Saturday, likewise in the northeast; and on a Monday, especially in the southeast. (10)
O Maheśānī, likewise, on the ninth lunar day, one setting out on a journey should not go toward the eastern region,
because the Yoginī is present face-to-face there.
One should likewise avoid the fourteenth and the sixth days for traveling to the west;
one should not go toward the southern direction on the thirteenth or the fifth day.
One should avoid the direction of the Rākṣasas on the second and the tenth [lunar days];
one should by all means abandon the northwestern direction on the full moon and the seventh.
One should not go toward the northeast on the new moon day or likewise on the eighth day;
one should avoid [starting a journey] on the first lunar day when the Viṣkumbha, Prīti, or Āyuṣmān yogas occur.
Know that Saubhāgya and Śobhana are in the second Gaṇḍaka, and Sukarmā and Dhṛti are in the third. || 15 ||
Gaṇḍa, Vṛddhi, Dhruva, and likewise Vyāghāta—
one should avoid these on the fourth day, O Goddess, as well as Harṣaṇa on the fifth.
O Śaṅkarī, know that Vajra and Siddhi occur on the sixth day during Vyatīpāta;
one should avoid Varīyān and Parigha on the seventh day. (17)
One should avoid Śiva, Siddhi, and Sādhya on the eighth lunar day (aṣṭamī);
on the ninth (navamī), one should avoid Śubha and Śukra; and on the tenth (daśamī), one should avoid Brahmā.
One should likewise avoid Indra on the eleventh day, Vaidhṛti on the twelfth, the three Uttarās on the thirteenth, and Viśākhā on the fourteenth. (19)
One should avoid Maghā, Ārdrā, and Bharaṇī on the full moon day; likewise, one should avoid Kṛttikā on the first lunar day (pratipad) and Jyeṣṭhā on the second lunar day.
One should never set out on a journey when the asterism is unfavorable; however, during an actual expedition, there is no need to consider whether the *karana* is auspicious or not.
One should always avoid [these acts] during the month of one's birth, on the day of one's birth, as well as under the constellation of one's birth,
and likewise on the eighth and ninth lunar days at all times.
Know that in times of distress and during travel, there is prosperity in the west;
and at the time of *godhūli*, know it to be in the east.
At midday it is in the south, at afternoon likewise in the north; at night it is in the northeast, and during the two twilights in the southwest.
At midday one should perform it in the southeast, and at dawn in the northwest;
during the yogas beginning with Vāruṇa, one should practice according to the proper time.
Except on one's birth day, and avoiding the eighth and ninth lunar days,
one should proceed toward the eastern direction and undertake the journey facing north.
In the west one should set out facing east; in the south, facing west;
and in the north, facing south—one should undertake a journey for the sake of perfect success.
